jobs.title: Vice President, Data & AI Engineering
jobs.text:
About Powerfleet Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.
Position Summary
Powerfleet is seeking a Vice President, Data & AI Engineering to lead the strategy, architecture, and execution of our enterprise Data & AI capabilities. This leader will help build the technology foundations that enable data-driven products, AI innovation, and greater productivity across the business.
The VP will lead teams across data engineering, AI/ML, GenAI, AI platforms, and intelligent automation, working closely with Product, Engineering, IT, Security, and business leaders. The role will balance strategic leadership with execution, helping Powerfleet move AI capabilities from experimentation into scalable, secure, and production-ready solutions.
Key Responsibilities
Define and execute Powerfleet’s Data & AI engineering strategy, roadmap, and priorities in alignment with business and product objectives.
Establish scalable, secure, and cost-effective architectures for enterprise data, AI/ML, GenAI, and AI-enabled applications.
Build a strong data foundation that supports analytics, machine learning, real-time intelligence, and AI use cases, promoting common platforms, reusable services, APIs, and engineering practices while enabling teams to innovate
Advise executive leadership on emerging AI capabilities, opportunities, risks, and technology investments.
Lead the development and adoption of capabilities across AI/ML, GenAI, AI agents, intelligent automation, and related technologies and establish practical frameworks and platforms that enable teams to move AI solutions from experimentation into production.
Advance MLOps/LLMOps, model evaluation, observability, governance, and other capabilities needed to operate AI reliably at scale.
Build and lead a high-performing global Data & AI engineering organization across relevant disciplines and geographies.
Partner with Security, Legal, Privacy, Risk, and other stakeholders to establish appropriate AI governance and responsible AI practices.
Establish appropriate metrics for platform adoption, engineering productivity, reliability, cost efficiency, and AI impact and manage technology investments, strategic vendors, and build-versus-buy decisions within the Data & AI domain.
Communicate strategy, progress, opportunities, and risks effectively to executive leadership and key stakeholders.
Qualifications
15+ years of experience in technology or engineering, with significant experience across data, software, cloud, platform, or AI engineering.
7+ years of leadership experience building and leading engineering teams, preferably in global or distributed organizations.
Experience developing enterprise data and AI platforms, architectures, and engineering strategies.
Strong understanding of modern data platforms, cloud technologies, data engineering, distributed systems, AI/ML, and software engineering.
Familiarity with modern GenAI patterns such as LLMs, RAG, agents, orchestration, evaluation, and AI observability.
Strong executive communication and the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
The annual salary range for this full-time position is $270,000-$300,000 USD. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on the candidate’s experience, skills, and location.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Powerfleet is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable law. We believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation and success, and we’re proud to be a workplace that reflects the communities we serve.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer - Remote (Americas time zones)
jobs.text:
This is a remote position.
Why this role exists
Sell2Rent is a fast-growing residential real estate platform specializing in sale-leaseback transactions. We help homeowners unlock their home equity without moving, while connecting properties with single-family rental investors. We operate in 30+ states and have closed 200+ transactions.
Technology is a key driver of our growth. We’ve built a proprietary operating platform, AI agents for lead qualification and outreach, an investor-matching layer, and a lead engine that supports our sales process.
We’re looking for a Chief Technology Officer (CTO) who sees technology as a growth and revenue engine — not just an engineering function. You’ll work closely with Sales, and Marketing, to use AI, automation, data, and product to generate more qualified leads, improve conversion, accelerate the sales cycle, and close more transactions.
You’ll inherit real, revenue-generating technology, a talented team, and the opportunity to create the technology strategy that will help Sell2Rent scale faster and sell more.
If you’re excited about using technology to drive measurable business results, this is your opportunity to make a major impact.
What you'll own
Technology strategy.You set the direction: architecture, build-vs-buy, which platforms we standardize on, where AI is a genuine advantage and where it's a distraction. You'll be the person in the room who knows what's actually possible and what it costs.
The engineering organization.You lead a distributed team of roughly ten across engineering and data, all of them in Latin America. You'll grow it, structure it, and set the bar.
Scaling the platform.Our twelve-month mandate is to ship the roadmap and scale what we've built — completing the migration off legacy systems, hardening the platform, and getting to a place where the business can grow transaction volume without engineering becoming the bottleneck.
The AI layer.Agents handle a meaningful share of our qualification, outreach, and internal operations today. Deciding how far that goes — and building it so it's a durable advantage rather than a demo — is one of the most interesting problems here.
Resilience and continuity.Security, access governance, vendor management, monitoring, documentation, and the discipline that ensures no single person is ever again the only one who knows how something works. We've learned this lesson the expensive way and we're not repeating it.
Executive partnership.You sit on the Executive Committee. You'll work directly with the CEO and the sales, marketing, and operations leaders — translating what the business needs into what gets built, and telling us honestly when what we're asking for is a bad idea.
Requirements
Who we're looking for
15+ years in technology, with progressive leadership responsibility and time as a CTO, VP of Engineering, or Head of Technology.
You've scaled a team and a system before.Not just managed one — took something from working-but-fragile to reliable-at-volume, and grew the org that did it.
You are technical enough to be trusted, but your job is not to write the code.You should be able to read our architecture, challenge a design decision, and evaluate a vendor on the merits. We have engineers to build. We need someone who can direct them and know when the answer is wrong.
Real depth in AI-driven architecture, cloud infrastructure (we run on GCP), APIs, integrations, and data. Depth, not enthusiasm — you can tell us what LLM-based agents actually break on in production.
You find blind spots.Much of the value in your first six months is telling us what we don't know we're missing — in our architecture, our tooling, our security posture, and our process.
You lead people well.Our team is remote, distributed, and international. Keeping engineers motivated, growing, and clear on what matters is a large part of this job.
Startup-fluent.You're comfortable with ambiguity, limited resources, and making decisions before all the information arrives.
Business-minded.You can connect a technical investment to revenue and defend it to a CEO who will ask.
Helpful, not required:real estate, proptech, or fintech experience; running a US-based company with a LatAm engineering team; Spanish.
How this role fits with product
Our CEO owns product direction and will continue to for the foreseeable future, working closely with the commercial leadership team. You own technology, architecture, and execution. You'll have real influence on what we build and strong input on sequencing — but the product roadmap is not yours to set, and we're not planning to hand it over.
We're stating this plainly because the previous version of this role blended both, and the wrong expectation here makes an otherwise great partnership fail. If owning a product is what you're looking for in your next role, this isn't it.
What success looks like
By 90 days— you know where every system, credential, vendor, and dependency lives, and so does someone besides you. You've told us the three things about our architecture that worry you most. The team knows who they report to, what they're building, and why it matters.
By 6 months— the platform migration is on a credible path, engineering has a real operating cadence, and technology decisions are being made deliberately rather than reactively. You've made at least one hire that raises the bar.
By 12 months— we've shipped the roadmap, the platform handles significantly more volume without more people, and our AI capability is a genuine competitive advantage rather than a set of internal tools. Nothing critical depends on any single individual, including you.
Benefits
Details
Location:Remote, with meaningful overlap with US Eastern and Latin America.
Compensation:Competitive base plus meaningful equity. We'll be direct about the range early in the process.
Team:~10 in technology and data; company-wide, a lean and fast-moving organization.
Our process
Intro call with the CEO — 45 minutes, mutual fit.
Technical and architectural conversation — we'll walk you through what we've actually built and get your honest read on it.
Meet the engineering team and two executive peers.
A working session on a real problem we're facing. Paid, if it requires meaningful preparation.
References and offer.
We move quickly and we'll tell you where you stand at every step.
Sell2Rent is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management (Security)
jobs.text:
Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.
We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.
Why You’ll Love This Role
Cribl just launched Cribl Detect, our SIEM built on the Cribl platform. Detection and response is the foundation. Your job is to figure out what comes next - and then build it.
As Director of Product Management for Security Products, you'll own the next wave of Cribl's security portfolio. You'll evaluate the most promising areas beyond Detect. You'll recommend which ones to pursue and in what order, with a clear case for build, partner, or buy. Then you'll lead what we fund, from the first customer conversations to launch and growth.
We'll be honest: the exact scope isn't fixed yet. That's the point. This role is for a product leader who wants to shape a portfolio, not inherit one - and who has the security depth to make the right calls.
As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…
Drive the strategy for the next wave of security products - market analysis, customer discovery, competitive landscape, and a clear recommendation on what to do first, second, and not at all.
Build the business case for each area - the customer problem, market size, why Cribl can win, build / partner / buy options, and what it takes to get there.
Lead execution for what we fund - define the product, write the requirements, set success metrics, and drive delivery with engineering from 0 to 1 and beyond.
Make it one platform - make sure new capabilities work natively with Cribl Detect (shared data model, detections, alerts, and workflows), not as a set of separate tools.
Spend real time with customers - CISOs, SOC managers, detection engineers, and analysts - and work with design partners to validate direction before we commit.
Partner with Marketing, Sales, and technology partners on positioning, packaging, launch, and field enablement.
Grow the team - as areas get funded, hire and lead product managers to own them.
Represent Cribl security externally with customers, analysts, and at industry events.
We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones - you may be required to occasionally perform duties outside your standard working hours.
If You’ve Got It - We Want It
10+ years in product management or a closely related role, with 5+ years building security products.
Deep understanding of security operations - SIEM, detection engineering, incident response, and how SOC teams actually work day to day.
Hands-on product experience in at least one of: security automation and response (SOAR), identity security (ITDR, UEBA), AI or agentic security, or threat detection and response.
A track record of taking a product from 0 to 1 - from problem discovery to a product customers pay for and use.
Portfolio-level thinking - you have evaluated new markets, built business cases, and made clear recommendations with incomplete information.
Leadership - experience leading or mentoring PMs, and leading through influence across engineering, marketing, and sales.
Technical depth to go deep with engineers on data architectures, detection logic, and AI/LLM-based systems.
Strong written communication - you write clear strategy docs and PRDs, and you make decisions in writing.
Good judgment under uncertainty - you can say "we shouldn't build this" as confidently as "we should."
Bonus Points
Earlier career experience on a security operations team (SOC, detection engineering, or incident response).
Experience with security data platforms, data pipelines, or security data lakes.
Experience with partner-led product strategy or M&A evaluation.
Familiarity with OCSF, KQL, and MITRE ATT&CK.
Experience working with security customers in both the US and Europe.
Experience in remote-first, distributed organizations.
No fear - speak your mind, share your ideas.
Good jokes (or better yet, bad ones).
A love for goats.
#LI-AM
#LI-Remote
The salary for this role is dependent on geographic location and will be based on the individual candidate's job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.
In addition to base salary, for sales and some sales-adjacent roles, employees are eligible to earn incentive compensation (commission). For all other roles, employees are eligible to participate in the Cribl Corporate Bonus Program.
In addition to a competitive salary, Cribl also offers a generous benefits package which includes health, dental, vision, short-term disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and paid time off, a fertility treatment benefit, 401(k), and equity.
Base Salary Range
$275,000—$310,000 USD
Bring Your Whole Self
Diversity drives innovation, enables better decisions to support our customers, and inspires change for the better. We’re building a culture where differences are valued and welcomed, and we work together to bring out the best in each other. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or any other applicable legally protected characteristics in the location in which the candidate is applying.
Interested in joining the Cribl herd? Learn more about the smartest, funniest, most passionate goats you’ll ever meet at cribl.io/about-us.

jobs.title: Director of Product Design
jobs.text:
We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.
We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.
After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us.
With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!
We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️
London / UK Remote | £140,000 - £165,000 + Equity + Benefits ✨
⭐ Our Design team
We’re a team of 115+ Product Designers, User Researchers, and Brand Designers led by Chief Design Officer Vuokko Aro. We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone. Product Design is the largest discipline within the design organisation, with designers working in tight-knit squads alongside researchers, product managers, and engineers to solve real customer problems at scale.
We design for the “magic moments.” We’ve built a bank that feels deeply human, not just functional, shaping how millions of people experience money every day. Our product is our personality. We combine research, empathy, and craft to turn everyday interactions into memorable experiences.
Now, we’re entering our next phase of growth and looking for exceptional design leaders to help define not only Monzo’s future, but the future of banking itself. There’s significant opportunity to shape the product, influence the organisation, and leave a lasting mark on millions of customers.
About the role
We’re looking for a Director of Product Design to lead design across Payments, one of Monzo’s most important and fast-evolving multi-market business areas.
You’ll partner closely with senior leaders across Product and Engineering to shape strategy, set direction, and drive exceptional execution across your area. You’ll play a key role in influencing the direction of both the product and the broader customer experience.
You’ll lead and grow a team of Product Designers, helping them do the best work of their careers while strengthening design thinking, collaboration, and craft across Monzo. As a senior leader within the Design organisation, you’ll raise the quality bar and expand design’s impact, influence, and effectiveness across Monzo.
You’ll play a key role by...
Setting the strategic direction and design vision for your area, inspiring teams to think bigger and bolder, whilst aligning with Monzo goals and mission.
Partnering with the leadership team for your area to define priorities, shape roadmaps, and turn strategy into impactful execution.
Building and nurturing a high-performing design team - investing in their growth, wellbeing, and long-term success.
Maintaining an exceptional quality bar across all design work through clear feedback and coaching, helping designers and teams consistently deliver best-in-class experiences.
Creating an environment where feedback is open, craft is celebrated, and design quality continues to evolve across the organisation.
Acting as a champion for design at Monzo, influencing how design thinking shapes our products and culture.
We’d love to hear from you if...
You’ve led design strategy and vision across complex product areas, helping teams navigate ambiguity and deliver meaningful customer and business impact.
You’re comfortable operating at multiple altitudes, from defining long-term direction to driving high-quality execution.
You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Research and Commercial, and know how to influence senior stakeholders through clarity, insight, and craft.
You have a strong point of view on product design and consistently raise the bar for quality, systems thinking, and customer experience.
You’ve built and led high-performing design teams, creating environments where people can grow, do exceptional work, and have meaningful impact.
You know how to scale design influence across an organisation, shaping product direction, ways of working, and culture beyond your immediate team.
You’re energised by Monzo’s mission to make money work for everyone, and excited to help shape the next generation of payments experiences through thoughtful, magical and innovative design.
What’s in it for you
£140,000 - £165,000 + Equity + Benefits
✈️ We’ll help you relocate to the UK
✅ We can sponsor your visa
This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London)
⏰ Flexible working hours and trust-based work culture
£1,000 annual learning budget for books, training, and conferences
Full remote setup support, including equipment and workspace essentials
➕ Plus lots more!
This process should take around 4-5 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible!
We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo. You can read them here.
We’ll only close this role once we have enough applications for the next stage. Please submit your application as soon as possible to make sure you don’t miss out.
#LI-TR1
#LI-Remote
Equal opportunities for everyone
Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of support for all of our people to grow at Monzo. At Monzo, we’re embracing diversity by fostering an inclusive environment for all people to do the best work of their lives with us. This is integral to our mission of making money work for everyone. You can read more in our blog, 2026 Diversity and Inclusion Report and 2025 Gender Pay Gap Report.
We’re an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, or veteran, neurodiversity or disability status.
If you have a preferred name, please use it to apply. We don't need full or birth names at application stage

jobs.title: Data Director, EU
jobs.text:
We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.
We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.
After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us.
With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!
We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️
London, Barcelona, or UK Remote | £150,900 to £204,100 + stock options & benefits | ✅ Visa sponsorship & relocation available
About our Data Discipline
We have a strong culture of data-driven decision making across the whole company. Data is central to how we understand our customers, shape our products, manage risk and grow Monzo sustainably. We believe in empowering teams with high-quality, trusted data and self-serve analytics, while creating space for Data practitioners to focus on the highest-impact questions, opportunities and decisions.
Our Data Discipline is deeply embedded in Monzo’s product areas. Data Scientists, Analytics Engineers, and Machine Learning Engineers work in cross-functional squads alongside Engineers, Designers, Product Managers and other disciplines. This means Data is not a downstream service, and instead we shape strategy, challenge thinking, build the data foundations teams need to move quickly, and share accountability for customer and commercial outcomes.
Our EU team ⭐
Our EU Data team is a full-stack Data team, and together we're building Monzo's presence across Europe from the ground up. We're entering new markets, learning what customers in each one need and finding product-market fit for Monzo.
Our mission is to make money work for everyone, everywhere. As Data Director for EU expansion you'll lead the Data team and shape our product strategy as we grow, deciding where we place our bets, working out what to measure before there's a playbook, and making sure each new market learns fast enough to compound into the next.
You'll work closely with EU leadership (our EU CEO, Country Managers and VP of Product) and Monzo's global Leadership team (the CTO, Head of Data and other Data Directors), sitting on the EU Tech Leadership team and helping shape our global data strategy. To do this well you'll need to relish ambiguity, bringing analytical rigour and commercial judgement to bets that often have to be made before the data is complete.
You’ll play a key role by...
You'll own the full learning loop that EU expansion runs on, and you'll co-own the product development loop alongside EU Leadership, Product and Engineering. In a new market that often means building those loops from scratch, so you're accountable not just for measuring what happens, but for framing the questions, defining what good looks like, and building the systems that answer them. You'll be a senior voice on the EU Tech Leadership team, the person who reframes the hard problems and puts a number on the trade-off between what's valuable for customers and what's valuable for the business.
Shaping product and commercial strategy:
You'll decide where Monzo should bet as we enter each new European market, sizing the opportunity and finding product-market fit for the products and segments most likely to win.
You'll use sharp commercial judgement to work through the ambiguity of building in a new market, from pricing and positioning to the levers that drive growth, bringing Data into strategy early so we shape priorities rather than react to decisions already made.
Owning the data strategy and the learning loops:
You'll set the data strategy for EU and stand up the foundations each new market needs, from the events we log and the metrics and experiments we design to the forecasts markets learn from.
Lead the goal-setting process for EU Expansion, bringing clarity to metric selection and target setting, in close partnership with Finance.
Changing how decisions get made:
You'll represent Data directly at the ExCo level, building a shared language of metrics and analytical reasoning so that Data drives EU strategy rather than reporting on it.
You'll drive cross-collective collaboration, spotting the high-leverage connections across the business, for example how savings features drive engagement in our Wealth collective.
Building and leading a high-performing team:
You'll build, grow and retain a high-performing, full-stack Data team, where everyone shares accountability for product and business outcomes.
You'll raise the performance bar, develop the next generation of Data leaders, and model an inclusive, high-craft Data culture as we scale.
We’d love to hear from you if…
What we're doing here at Monzo excites you, and the idea of helping take it across Europe especially so!
You're a strategic data leader who has operated at Director level or above, and you're energised by zero-to-one ambiguity, having built or scaled a data function in a new market, product line or business from an early stage.
You move comfortably from detailed metrics and data architecture to customer strategy, commercial outcomes and product-market fit, and you're happy to be the opinionated voice in the room that reframes the trade-off.
You lead through learning loops and hold a high technical bar, because you've built or owned the measurement a business relies on to set goals, run experiments and improve, with the judgement to know which methods and investments will pay off.
You have experience leading company-wide or division-wide goal-setting, defining high-clarity metrics, setting targets and partnering closely with Finance.
You change how organisations make decisions, not just how one project turns out, and you have experience of the cross-collective collaboration that connects the dots across different business areas.
You're an empathetic people leader who has grown full-stack Data teams of both individual contributors and managers, comfortable representing Data at ExCo and to C-level peers, and you know what it takes to attract, develop and retain top talent.
The application journey has 4 key steps
30 minute recruiter call
45 minute call with the hiring manager
4 x 1-hour video calls with various team members, including the General Manager for Payments
A meet and greet with a member of EU Executive Committee
Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability.
What’s in it for you:
What’s in it for you
£150,900 to £204,100 + stock options and benefits
✅ We can sponsor visas
This role can be based in our London or Barcelona office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London)
⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team
Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences
We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup.
➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits.

Translate between technical, product and commercial perspectives to help teams make clear, high-impact decisions

What we’re doing here at Monzo excites you!

The Interview Process
After an informal ~30 min recruiter call, our interview process involves 2 main stages. We promise not to ask you any brain teasers or trick questions!
Initial Call (1 hour) You'll meet with one of our senior data leaders.
Loop Stage - This is one stage with 4 interviews (totalling 4 hours) split between a collaboration with one of our engineers on a technical exercise, as well as behavioural and leadership interviews. You can have this all in one day or split these across multiple days, whichever your prefer.
Our average process takes around 3-4 weeks but we will always work around your availability. You will have the chance to speak to our recruitment team at various points during your process but if you do have any specific questions ahead of this please contact us on tech-hiring@monzo.com
How we work :
Locations & Flexible Working :
Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles.
We value meeting in person but there’s no pressure to come into the office, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨
Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays ️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.
Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life.
At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance.
You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. ✨
Work the way that works for you with Monzo!

Base salary £150, 000 - £200, 000 + Equity + Benefits
✈️ We can help you relocate to the UK

This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London).

Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences

blocks.text: We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.
We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us.

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!
We’re not about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo ❤️
London or UK Remote | £150,000 - £200, 000 + Equity + Benefits
About our Data Discipline

We have a strong culture of data-driven decision making across the whole company. Data is central to how we understand our customers, shape our products, manage risk and grow Monzo sustainably. We believe in empowering teams with high-quality, trusted data and self-serve analytics, while creating space for Data practitioners to focus on the highest-impact questions, opportunities and decisions.

Our Data discipline is centralised, but deeply embedded in Monzo’s product areas. Data Scientists, Analytics Engineers, Machine Learning Engineers and Analysts work in cross-functional squads alongside Engineers, Designers, Product Managers, Marketers and other specialists. This means Data is not a downstream service: we help shape strategy, challenge thinking, build the data foundations teams need to move quickly, and share accountability for customer and commercial outcomes.
Our Payments team ⭐

At Monzo, payments are more than just moving money from A to B. They are a core part of how customers experience trust, speed, and financial control every day. As a Data Director in Payments, you would help shape seamless local payment experiences, ensuring customers can pay and get paid reliably while continuing to modernise the infrastructure that powers millions of transactions behind the scenes.

The role also sits at the intersection of Monzo’s broader ambition to build truly borderless banking and expand into new markets. That means designing products and payment capabilities that work effortlessly across geographies, currencies, and customer needs, while helping Monzo scale into new markets with the same simplicity and transparency that defines the brand today.

You’ll partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Design to help shape Monzo’s payments strategy to make Monzo's global ambitions a reality, enabling revenue and customer growth with a resilient, self-serve banking platform.
To succeed, you should be excited about solving tough, ambiguous business problems with analytical rigour, commercial viability and execution effectiveness

jobs.title: Fractional Director of Technology (Advisor Network)
jobs.text:
Opportunity Overview
Arootah engages a curated network of senior operators to support clients across the alternative investment industry, including hedge funds, private equity firms, and family offices. Advisors are deployed on project-based engagements when client needs match their expertise. Joining the network does not guarantee placement; it provides access to opportunities as they arise.
Why Join the Arootah Network
Alt-industry-only engagements with hedge funds, private equity firms, and family offices
Project-based work that fits around existing commitments
Client origination and engagement management handled by Arootah; advisors focus on delivery
About Arootah
Arootah is a talent solutions firm purpose-built for the alternative investment industry. We advise and we execute, covering the full talent spectrum from entry to exit across five services: Talent Acquisition, Fractional Leadership, Talent Development, Retention & Compensation, and Transition.
Most talent firms solve one problem. Because we cover the full spectrum, we can help clients identify and solve the right one. We start with diagnosis, then deliver.
Our team has run alternative investment firms at the highest levels as COOs, CFOs, and CCOs. That operator experience, combined with 15+ years of alternatives-specific recruiting and a network of 700+ vetted advisors across 18 functional disciplines, is what makes the advice credible and the execution reliable. We also draw on a network of 600+ coaches, deploying those with specific experience guiding senior executives in the alternatives industry.
One industry. One talent partner. Entry to exit.
Learn more:
Who We’re Looking For
Arootah is searching for experienced Directors of Technology to consult to our highly prestigious client base. As a consultant, you will work with our Alternative Asset Firm and Family Office clients to provide expert advice. Having previously served in this leadership role, you have specific, hands-on experience strategically supporting the efforts of the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) in building, maintaining, and overseeing the full technology (hardware and software) infrastructure and operations of a leading Alternative Asset Firm or Family Office.
Core Areas of Expertise
Best practice reviews.
Developing realistic and effective action plans.
Breaking apart goals into actionable steps.
Advising on vendor selection and oversight.
Creating and implementing policies, procedures, and control measures.
Evaluating each client’s advancement toward goal actualization through key performance indicators (KPIs) and scoring matrices.
Special projects or other areas of need.
Assist and support the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) in managing all aspects of the day-to-day management and oversight of the full tech stack across the organization: software (full stack, mobile/web apps, AR/VR, metaverse), hardware (IT, IoT, connected devices), cybersecurity, operations (internal, external), policies, etc.
Lead and manage the design, development, and deployment of new applications, systems software, and/or enhancements to existing applications.
Ensure application optimization and transformation to enable corporate partners continued business growth and expansion.
Supervise and implement a proactive cybersecurity, disaster recovery and business continuity planning mindset across the firm to maintain industry-leading uptime on critical technology infrastructure through successful monitoring, testing processes, and system redundancy.
Provide resource management and communication across multiple product and engagement teams that rely on and are impacted by technology. Support and influence user adoption and user understanding, such as through training and demos.
Optimize and supervise IT infrastructure to ensure integrity, security, and optimal performance of an office-based and remote, distributed, and growing team of employees and contractors to the standards of leading financial service organizations.
Oversee and provide technical direction, management support and daily guidance to IT staff, ensuring adherence to technology policies, security controls, regulatory requirements, and company policies.
Working with the CTO, establish and monitor KPIs to continuously track, measure, and drive productivity.
Generate new ideas and creative solutions to complex business problems; support the development of technology roadmaps that align with business current and future needs.
Advise CTO and senior leadership on issues affecting the operations and/or strategic direction of the Technology team.
What You Bring
A Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
MBA or other relevant graduate degree is a plus.
6+ years of proven experience as a Director of Technology at an Alternative Asset Firm or family office.
Strong technical knowledge and expertise in all facets of IT, including Application Teams, Information Security, Business Process Management, Program and Portfolio Management, IT Partner and Supplier Management, IT Architecture Management, Digital Platforms, and IT Infrastructure and Operations.
Strong experience with Investment Technology vendors for both hosted and on-prem platforms. This could include derivatives platforms (e.g. Calypso, Murex), investment accounting platforms (e.g. Eagle, ePam), OMS vendors (e.g. Aladdin, CRD) and others (e.g. Bloomberg, FactSet).
Expertise in budget & resource planning/monitoring to ensure budget optimization.
Strong understanding of the business processes in the regulated environment of investment management and financial services firms.
Ability to collaborate and succeed in a fast-paced environment while maintaining focus on on-time delivery, customer satisfaction (both internal and external) and team morale.

jobs.title: Head of Data & Analytics
jobs.text:
Salary: up to £88,250 depending on experience (Band 4)
Our first shop opened in 1981 in Penzance, selling durable clothing to artists and mariners. Today, we’re a modern, data-enabled omnichannel retailer with a growing international presence. We blend heritage with innovation, designing timeliness clothing made from responsibility sourced fabrics, and using technology to improve how we operate, grow and serve customers.
As we scale in the UK and internationally (primarily through third-party partnerships), we’re investing in data, systems and digital capability to support our people and our growth. It’s an exciting time to join us!
As the Head of Data & Analytics, you will lead the vision, strategy, architecture, governance, and delivery of data services across Seasalt. Overseeing the data engineering and analytics teams, you’ll ensure data is an enabler of innovation, decision-making, and commercial success in a fast-paced fashion retail environment.
This role will drive the development of a modern data platform (MDP) leveraging Azure technologies, ensuring robust data governance and assurance, and enabling enterprise-wide access to trustworthy, high-quality insights through SQL-based data warehousing, Synapse, Fabric, and PowerBI.
Please note that internally, this role will be referred to as ‘Senior Data Services Manager’.
Please note this role is based remotely within the UK, with occasional travel to our Cornwall head offices.
You’ll help us by:
Defining and championing a forward-looking data strategy aligned with the business's digital transformation and commercial priorities.
Translating business requirements into scalable data service roadmaps, ensuring alignment across product, technology, and analytics teams.
Managing and developing a high-performing team of data engineers and analysts by setting clear goals, fostering technical excellence and ensuring efficient delivery across agile cycles.
Gaining a deep understanding of our on-premises data warehouse built using SSIS and SSRS and incorporate this knowledge to drive the decommissioning and migration strategy as part of the Data Transformation programme.
Selecting and leading the delivery of technologies to deliver resilient, scalable and future-proofed data solutions, following good practice analytics architecture development
Owning the architectural design and evolution of the enterprise data platform on Azure (Synapse, Fabric, Data Lake, etc.) as well as the operational DWH.
Ensuring secure, efficient, and scalable data pipelines and integrations between systems using modern best practices.
Overseeing the management and enhancement of SQL data warehouses to meet operational and reporting needs.
Establishing and overseeing data quality standards, assurance frameworks, and compliance practices while ensuring adoption of data governance, assurance and ownership throughout the organisation through a network of data owners and stewards.
Ensuring robust governance of data models, metadata, and data cataloguing for internal and external reporting needs.
Monitoring and optimising Power BI data models and performance, ensuring business teams have access to reliable and timely insights.
Partnering with commercial and operational leads to enable self-serve reporting, data literacy, and data democratisation.
The skills you’ll be sharing with the team:
Degree or equivalent experience in: Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Mathematics/Statistics or a closely related discipline.
Proven experience leading data engineering, analytics, or data platform functions in a commercial environment, ideally retail.
Experienced leader, able to provide direction, motivate and inspire teams to support career growth.
Strategic thinker, able to define and communicate a compelling data vision, translate business needs into data strategies, and prioritise accordingly at pace.
Strong ability to guide data engineers and analysts in building scalable, secure, and reliable cloud data platforms, particularly using Azure, Synapse, SQL DWH, and Power BI.
Excellent communication skills, capable of building trust with commercial, technology, and executive stakeholders.
Experience enabling self-serve BI and building strong relationships with business functions using Power BI or similar tools.
Track record of delivery oversight, able to manage projects, allocate resources effectively, and deliver high-quality data services in agile or iterative environments.
Strong problem solver, able to understand complexities, tackle challenges effectively and quickly identify solutions.
Commercial acumen to understand how data impacts business KPIs and how to align technical decisions with commercial outcomes.
Cloud and integration expertise (e.g. Azure Data Lake, Fabric, ADF, Databricks, Logic Apps)
Desirable certifications include: Microsoft Azure Data Engineer Associate, Power BI Data Analyst (PL-300), Databricks/dbt/Synapse training
Why we hope you’ll love working with us:
The success of Seasalt is down to the skill and hard work of our team. We don't just want to attract the best and brightest people to come and work with us, we want you to stay and grow with us.
As well as doing everything we can to support your development professionally, we believe encouraging personal growth is just as important. So you can fulfil your passion and purpose, not just at work but in life, we offer a range of benefits that are designed to enhance your career and wellbeing:
34 days paid annual leave (including bank holidays), increasing with length of service
Attractive 50% employee discount
Flexible benefits allowance to personalise your benefits package
Private Medical Scheme including 24/7 virtual GP
Free access to our Employee Assistance Programme through Retail Trust with 24/7 support
Pension plan with generous 7% employer contributions
Life assurance programme
Enhanced family leave policies
Flexible working opportunities with our hybrid working approach
Learning and Development opportunities
Do Good Things with our two days per year paid volunteering opportunities
Employee networks to develop and provide support to our people, including the Inclusion & Belonging Network
100s of savings on top retailers and gym memberships through our discount hub
At Seasalt we have a brilliant team of people – they're what make Seasalt a fantastic place to work. We love to celebrate uniqueness and are committed to making Seasalt a place where everyone feels they belong. As an inclusive employer, we want to invite a diverse range of candidates to apply for our roles.
We aim to work flexibly where possible and value a range of perspectives - diversity of thought helps us to grow – so please apply if this is a role that would make you excited to come to work every day. We're happy to help with any adjustments to our recruitment process and beyond. Just drop us an email at
Closing date for applications is 29th October 2026, however our roles can close earlier so we would recommend applying as soon as you are able.

Arootah engages a curated network of senior operators to support clients across the alternative investment industry, including hedge funds, private equity firms, and family offices. Advisors are deployed on project-based engagements when client needs match their expertise. Joining the network does not guarantee placement; it provides access to opportunities as they arise.

Alt-industry-only engagements with hedge funds, private equity firms, and family offices
Project-based work that fits around existing commitments
Client origination and engagement management handled by Arootah; advisors focus on delivery
About Arootah
Arootah is a talent solutions firm purpose-built for the alternative investment industry. We advise and we execute, covering the full talent spectrum from entry to exit across five services: Talent Acquisition, Fractional Leadership, Talent Development, Retention & Compensation, and Transition.
Most talent firms solve one problem. Because we cover the full spectrum, we can help clients identify and solve the right one. We start with diagnosis, then deliver.
Our team has run alternative investment firms at the highest levels as COOs, CFOs, and CCOs. That operator experience, combined with 15+ years of alternatives-specific recruiting and a network of 700+ vetted advisors across 18 functional disciplines, is what makes the advice credible and the execution reliable. We also draw on a network of 600+ coaches, deploying those with specific experience guiding senior executives in the alternatives industry.
One industry. One talent partner. Entry to exit.

Who We’re Looking For
Arootah is seeking experienced Chief Technology Officers and senior technology leaders to join our advisor network and support clients across the alternative investment landscape.

Building, modernizing, and optimizing technology infrastructure across alternative investment firms
Overseeing systems architecture, cloud strategy, cybersecurity, and enterprise technology operations
Driving technology transformation, automation, and operational efficiency initiatives

Managing technology risk, business continuity, and data security frameworks

Prior experience as a Chief Technology Officer or equivalent senior technology leadership role within a hedge fund, private equity firm, family office, or financial services organization
Deep understanding of investment management technology infrastructure and operating environments
Proven track record of leading technology transformation and scaling enterprise systems
Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills

jobs.title: Director of Product, AML & Digital Asset Compliance
jobs.text:
About the Company
Born from groundbreaking research at Columbia University and Yale University, CertiK is a leading Web3 security company focused on securing blockchain protocols, smart contracts, and decentralized applications through cutting-edge security research, formal verification, and AI-powered technology. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in New York City, CertiK provides end-to-end security solutions including smart contract audits, penetration testing, on-chain monitoring, incident response, and compliance services for some of the largest projects in the digital asset ecosystem. Today, CertiK supports thousands of enterprise clients and Web3 projects globally, with a distributed international team spanning North America, Asia, and Europe. The company is backed by leading investors including Coatue, Goldman Sachs, Insight Partners, and Sequoia Capital, and has been recognized by organizations such as the World Economic Forum and CB Insights for its contributions to blockchain security innovation.
CertiK has spent years building security, risk, monitoring, and blockchain expertise across thousands of digital asset companies and institutional customers. As digital assets increasingly become part of mainstream financial infrastructure, security, financial crime risk, and regulatory compliance are converging. We believe there is an opportunity to build a new generation of institutional digital asset risk and compliance products at that intersection. This role will have significant influence over what that product becomes. We are looking for someone who wants to build it.
About the Role
CertiK is building the next generation of risk and compliance products for financial institutions and digital asset businesses. We are looking for a product leader to own this product area from customer discovery and product strategy through delivery, go to market, adoption, and expansion. This is not an internal compliance role. You are here to build the products that compliance, AML, financial crime, and risk teams use. You will work directly with financial institutions, exchanges, VASPs, fintechs, and other digital asset businesses to understand how their compliance teams operate, identify the problems that matter most, and turn those problems into scalable products. The product space may include areas such as blockchain and entity risk, transaction and wallet monitoring, sanctions and KYT, risk scoring, investigation and case management workflows, continuous monitoring, and compliance evidence and reporting. A core part of your job will be deciding which problems CertiK should solve first and which ones we should not. You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Compliance, Business Development, and company leadership to build this product line.
Responsibilities
Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for CertiK's AML and digital asset compliance products.
Spend significant time with customers and prospective customers, including CCOs, MLROs, AML teams, investigators, and risk leaders, to deeply understand their workflows and unmet needs.
Identify repeatable market problems behind individual customer requests and determine which problems should become scalable products.
Translate customer and market insights into product concepts, prototypes, requirements, and clear engineering priorities.
Drive products from discovery through design, development, launch, adoption, and iteration.
Define the key workflows, risk models, decision systems, and user experiences required by institutional compliance teams.
Work closely with Engineering and Data teams to make appropriate product and technical trade offs.
Partner with Business Development and customer facing teams during strategic sales cycles, including discovery, product demonstrations, pilots, and design partnerships.
Work with Compliance and regulatory experts to translate evolving AML, sanctions, and digital asset requirements into scalable product capabilities.
Measure success through customer adoption, product usage, enterprise wins, expansion, and other measurable business outcomes.
Requirements
Significant product management experience building B2B software in fintech, regtech, financial services, risk, compliance, or digital assets.
A track record of owning meaningful products or product areas from discovery through launch and adoption.
Deep understanding of AML, financial crime, transaction monitoring, sanctions, KYC/KYB, investigations, or related compliance workflows.
Experience building or working closely with products such as transaction monitoring, blockchain analytics, wallet screening, risk engines, case management, investigation platforms, or compliance workflow systems.
Strong customer discovery skills. You can speak credibly with senior compliance leaders and frontline analysts, understand both what they say and what they actually need, and translate those insights into product decisions.
Strong product judgment. You know the difference between a one off customer request and a repeatable market need, and you are comfortable making hard prioritization decisions.
Commercial instincts. You understand that a successful enterprise product must not only work, customers must adopt it, pay for it, and expand their usage.
Ability to operate in an ambiguous, early stage product environment and personally drive work forward rather than simply coordinate across teams.
Bonus Points
Experience building AML or compliance products at a blockchain analytics, fintech, regtech, exchange, bank, or financial infrastructure company.
Experience with blockchain analytics, KYT, wallet screening, on chain investigations, or digital asset risk.
Previous experience as an AML practitioner, compliance officer, MLRO, investigator, or financial crime professional.
Experience working with regulated financial institutions and understanding how compliance products are evaluated, procured, implemented, and operated.
Experience with regulatory examinations, VASP licensing, or financial crime remediation.
CAMS or another relevant professional qualification.
Relationships with compliance and risk leaders across banks, fintechs, exchanges, VASPs, regulators, or law enforcement.
Compensation
Additional Information
The expected annual base salary range for this position in the United States is $150,000 to $220,000. Compensation for candidates outside the United States will be determined based on location, experience, and qualifications.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product and Technology
jobs.text:
Senior Director, Product and Technology
Location: Remote,
Application Submission Deadline: November 1, 2026
About Us
Propel America addresses a broken workforce system that fails both young adults and healthcare employers, sidelining talented individuals from entering healthcare careers and contributing to critical workforce shortages that threaten community health. Propel’s work centers on bridging this gap by creating alternative, debt-free career pathways into healthcare for young adults ages 18–26, particularly those from underrepresented and low-income backgrounds, while helping employers access the trained, diverse talent they urgently need. Today, over 13 million young adults in the U.S. are either not in school, not working, or stuck in low-wage jobs with little room for growth. Traditional college remains financially and logistically out of reach for many, especially young people from low-income communities, forcing them into a false choice: sacrifice income to pursue an expensive degree or remain in low-wage work without upward mobility. At the same time, systemic barriers, such as limited exposure to healthcare roles, low visibility of alternative pathways, and a lack of representative mentors, prevent many high school graduates from entering the healthcare field.
Meanwhile, healthcare employers face compounding workforce shortages. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects a 13% growth in healthcare jobs from 2021 to 2031, translating to nearly 2 million openings annually. Many of these are middle-skill roles, which represent over half the U.S. labor market but remain unfilled due to a lack of training infrastructure. Employers often contend with high turnover in entry-level positions yet underinvest in structured career advancement pathways or innovative strategies to retain talent.
Propel America aims to solve both sides of the equation, by equipping young adults with the skills and support to launch healthcare careers and by helping employers build stronger, more diverse, and more stable workforces. In our portfolio, we offer a suite of Propel Paths and Propel Products to place young adults in critical talent gaps in healthcare
To learn more about Propel America, please visit .
The Opportunity
Propel America is undergoing an exciting phase of growth and technological transformation, marked by the development of our signature Fellow Portal and the integration of cutting-edge AI technologies into our program delivery. To lead this effort, we are seeking a highly skilled and strategic Director, Product and Technology.
This role sits within our newly formed Solutions Team and reports directly to the Vice President of Solutions.
The Director will serve as our core technology lead, managing the technical implementation of our product roadmap, maintaining the integrity of our overall technology stack, and directly supervising our technical staff (Salesforce Administrator and Junior Product Developer).
Key Responsibilities
The ideal candidate is a product developer who can set a vision and design the technology roadmap while also architecting integrations, managing developers and salesforce administration as well as overseeing outsourced Managed Service Providers (MSPs). The Direct will act as the critical link between Propel’s strategic vision and our day-to-day software execution, ensuring that our infrastructure is secure, scalable, and built to support our fellows' journey
Key Responsibilities include
Product leadership 40%
Technology stack management and development 40%
Cross Functional Collaboration (20%)
Product Leadership
Develop technology roadmap and set vision for Propel’s technology products including the Applicant and Fellow Portal to ensure they are responsive to fellows and employer needs
Directly manage the Junior Product Developer in building and iterating on the Fellow Portal, ensuring coding standards, version control, and security practices are rigorously maintained.
Guide the technical implementation of AI-integrated tools within the Fellow Portal to accelerate development, improve portal functionality, and enhance the user experience.
Establish and enforce development workflows (e.g., Agile Scrum/Kanban, code reviews, deployment pipelines) to minimize technical debt and streamline release cycles.
Work collaboratively with the VP of Solutions and key stakeholders to translate strategic product requirements into clear, prioritized technical backlogs.
Work closely with Director, Content Solutions and Product Director, Apprenticeship to develop technology requirements for Propel suite of products including PropelRecruit, Apprenticeship, TTE and Hire Ready Content.
Define and track success measures for the Fellow Portal and other products, such as adoption, engagement, completion and time-to-placement.
Run discovery with fellows, applicants and employers (interviews, usability testing, feedback loops).
Oversee QA, testing, release management and technical documentation.
2. Tech Stack Management & Architecture
Own the strategic and operational direction of IT infrastructure, software development, and data systems
Ensure the reliability, scalability, and security of core enterprise systems (Salesforce, Google Cloud, Forms software, virtual private servers, website hosting, code management workflows).
Lead architecture and platform decisions in partnership with VP, Solutions.
Evaluate and select software and vendors, and negotiate contracts and renewals
Directly manage the Salesforce Administrator to ensure Propel's CRM is optimized to support programmatic operations, student tracking, and data-driven decision-making
Conduct regular audits of the organizational tech stack to eliminate overlaps, consolidate licenses, and ensure optimal data flow across departments.
Define and implement standards for cybersecurity, information security, and data privacy, safeguarding fellow, staff, and donor data, including oversight of all data flows between systems (e.g. FERPA, health information and funder requirements)
Act as the primary technical point of contact and relationship manager for Propel’s outsourced Managed IT Service Provider
Ensure the MSP successfully resolves Level 1 help desk tickets, user account maintenance, and daily IT support requests, completely offloading this burden from Propel’s executive leadership
Collaborate with the MSP to maintain healthy network infrastructure, ensure data backups and disaster recovery plans are active, and manage device lifecycles
Identify budgetary needs for technology and work closely VP, Solutions to develop the annual budget
Set responsible-AI guidelines, covering acceptable use, data handling, bias review and human oversight.
3. Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner closely with the entire solutions team to support the integration of technology into the development of products and solutions
Work closely with the Senior Director of Evaluation and Learning to ensure that Salesforce is the source of truth for all data
Work closely with with the Partnerships team to ensure that employer and fellow feedback is incorporated into the technology priorities and solutions development
Lead technology team to support cross functional and organization priorities by modeling Propel’s core values
Train staff on systems and lead change management when tools are rolled out.
Required Qualifications
Product Development: 6-8 years in product or technology, including 3+ years managing people; experience in discovery, writing and developing technology requirements and bringing products to market
People Management: Demonstrated experience directly managing technical staff (developers, database admins, or system engineers) and fostering a collaborative, high-performance team culture
Platform & CRM Familiarity: Deep understanding of the Salesforce ecosystem, database schemas, and cloud-based integrations
Vendor Coordination: Proven track record of managing technology vendors, software developers, and external IT consultants or MSPs
Modern Workflows: Strong familiarity with Agile software development methodologies (Scrum/Kanban)
APIs: Experience leveraging AI, APIs or machine learning integration in customer-facing products
Data security: Experience with managing PII and other secure data
Preferred Qualifications
Prior experience working in the nonprofit, workforce development, or education technology (EdTech) sectors
Product engineering experience or knowledge of coding
Salesforce certification (Admin, Platform App Builder), or Nonprofit/Education Cloud experience
Experience designing products for young adults or mobile-first users
Experience with low-code/no-code tools
Success Profile
Strategic Translator: Exceptional ability to translate education and business requirements into pragmatic, scalable technology plans
Security & Risk-Minded: Practical understanding of cybersecurity protocols, access control frameworks, and compliance auditing
Clear Communicator: Outstanding verbal and written communication skills, with a focus on simplicity, clarity, and active listening, and effective collaboration across functional teams.
Mission-Driven: Strong alignment with Propel America’s values of innovation, courage, joy, team, equity, and impact
Compensation
The salary for this position is between $113,000-$153,200 annually. We consider candidate experience and location when determining where a candidate may fall within that range. Propel America offers a competitive total rewards package including coverage of 90% of health insurance premiums, unlimited PTO, and a flexible work environment.
Interested in applying?
Please submit your application here.The application deadline to apply for this position is November 1, 2026. After this date we do not guarantee review of submissions.
Propel America is an equal-opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.
We encourage candidates from historically underrepresented backgrounds to apply.
Salary: $113,000 – $153,200 / year

At the same time, systemic barriers, such as limited exposure to healthcare roles, low visibility of alternative pathways, and a lack of representative mentors, prevent many high school graduates from entering the healthcare field.

Meanwhile, healthcare employers face compounding workforce shortages. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects a 13% growth in healthcare jobs from 2021 to 2031, translating to nearly 2 million openings annually. Many of these are middle-skill roles, which represent over half the U.S. labor market but remain unfilled due to a lack of training infrastructure. Employers often contend with high turnover in entry-level positions yet underinvest in structured career advancement pathways or innovative strategies to retain talent.

Propel America aims to solve both sides of the equation, by equipping young adults with the skills and support to launch healthcare careers and by helping employers build stronger, more diverse, and more stable workforces. In our portfolio, we offer a suite of Propel Paths and Propel Products to place young adults in critical talent gaps in healthcare
To learn more about Propel America, please visit .
The Opportunity

Propel America is undergoing an exciting phase of growth and technological transformation, marked by the development of our signature Fellow Portal and the integration of cutting-edge AI technologies into our program delivery. To lead this effort, we are seeking a highly skilled and strategic Director, Product and Technology.
This role sits within our newly formed Solutions Team and reports directly to the Vice President of Solutions.

The Director will serve as our core technology lead, managing the technical implementation of our product roadmap, maintaining the integrity of our overall technology stack, and directly supervising our technical staff (Salesforce Administrator and Junior Product Developer).
Key Responsibilities

The ideal candidate is a product developer who can set a vision and design the technology roadmap while also architecting integrations, managing developers and salesforce administration as well as overseeing outsourced Managed Service Providers (MSPs). The Direct will act as the critical link between Propel’s strategic vision and our day-to-day software execution, ensuring that our infrastructure is secure, scalable, and built to support our fellows' journey
Key Responsibilities include

items: Product leadership 40%
Technology stack management and development 40%
Cross Functional Collaboration (20%)

blocks.text: Product Leadership

items: Develop technology roadmap and set vision for Propel’s technology products including the Applicant and Fellow Portal to ensure they are responsive to fellows and employer needs
Directly manage the Junior Product Developer in building and iterating on the Fellow Portal, ensuring coding standards, version control, and security practices are rigorously maintained.
Guide the technical implementation of AI-integrated tools within the Fellow Portal to accelerate development, improve portal functionality, and enhance the user experience.
Establish and enforce development workflows (e.g., Agile Scrum/Kanban, code reviews, deployment pipelines) to minimize technical debt and streamline release cycles.
Work collaboratively with the VP of Solutions and key stakeholders to translate strategic product requirements into clear, prioritized technical backlogs.

Work closely with Director, Content Solutions and Product Director, Apprenticeship to develop technology requirements for Propel suite of products including PropelRecruit, Apprenticeship, TTE and Hire Ready Content.
Define and track success measures for the Fellow Portal and other products, such as adoption, engagement, completion and time-to-placement.
Run discovery with fellows, applicants and employers (interviews, usability testing, feedback loops).
Oversee QA, testing, release management and technical documentation.

blocks.text: 2. Tech Stack Management & Architecture

items: Own the strategic and operational direction of IT infrastructure, software development, and data systems
Ensure the reliability, scalability, and security of core enterprise systems (Salesforce, Google Cloud, Forms software, virtual private servers, website hosting, code management workflows).
Lead architecture and platform decisions in partnership with VP, Solutions.
Evaluate and select software and vendors, and negotiate contracts and renewals
Directly manage the Salesforce Administrator to ensure Propel's CRM is optimized to support programmatic operations, student tracking, and data-driven decision-making
Conduct regular audits of the organizational tech stack to eliminate overlaps, consolidate licenses, and ensure optimal data flow across departments.

Define and implement standards for cybersecurity, information security, and data privacy, safeguarding fellow, staff, and donor data, including oversight of all data flows between systems (e.g. FERPA, health information and funder requirements)
Act as the primary technical point of contact and relationship manager for Propel’s outsourced Managed IT Service Provider
Ensure the MSP successfully resolves Level 1 help desk tickets, user account maintenance, and daily IT support requests, completely offloading this burden from Propel’s executive leadership
Collaborate with the MSP to maintain healthy network infrastructure, ensure data backups and disaster recovery plans are active, and manage device lifecycles
Identify budgetary needs for technology and work closely VP, Solutions to develop the annual budget
Set responsible-AI guidelines, covering acceptable use, data handling, bias review and human oversight.

blocks.text: 3. Cross-Functional Collaboration

items: Partner closely with the entire solutions team to support the integration of technology into the development of products and solutions
Work closely with the Senior Director of Evaluation and Learning to ensure that Salesforce is the source of truth for all data
Work closely with with the Partnerships team to ensure that employer and fellow feedback is incorporated into the technology priorities and solutions development
Lead technology team to support cross functional and organization priorities by modeling Propel’s core values
Train staff on systems and lead change management when tools are rolled out.

blocks.text: Required Qualifications

items: Product Development: 6-8 years in product or technology, including 3+ years managing people; experience in discovery, writing and developing technology requirements and bringing products to market
People Management: Demonstrated experience directly managing technical staff (developers, database admins, or system engineers) and fostering a collaborative, high-performance team culture
Platform & CRM Familiarity: Deep understanding of the Salesforce ecosystem, database schemas, and cloud-based integrations
Vendor Coordination: Proven track record of managing technology vendors, software developers, and external IT consultants or MSPs
Modern Workflows: Strong familiarity with Agile software development methodologies (Scrum/Kanban)
APIs: Experience leveraging AI, APIs or machine learning integration in customer-facing products
Data security: Experience with managing PII and other secure data

blocks.text: Preferred Qualifications

items: Prior experience working in the nonprofit, workforce development, or education technology (EdTech) sectors
Product engineering experience or knowledge of coding
Salesforce certification (Admin, Platform App Builder), or Nonprofit/Education Cloud experience
Experience designing products for young adults or mobile-first users
Experience with low-code/no-code tools

blocks.text: Success Profile

items: Strategic Translator: Exceptional ability to translate education and business requirements into pragmatic, scalable technology plans
Security & Risk-Minded: Practical understanding of cybersecurity protocols, access control frameworks, and compliance auditing
Clear Communicator: Outstanding verbal and written communication skills, with a focus on simplicity, clarity, and active listening, and effective collaboration across functional teams.
Mission-Driven: Strong alignment with Propel America’s values of innovation, courage, joy, team, equity, and impact

blocks.text: Compensation

The salary for this position is between $113,000-$153,200 annually. We consider candidate experience and location when determining where a candidate may fall within that range. Propel America offers a competitive total rewards package including coverage of 90% of health insurance premiums, unlimited PTO, and a flexible work environment.

jobs.title: Director of Data, Strategy & Performance
jobs.text:
Harlem Children’s Zone (HCZ) — a world-renowned education and poverty-fighting organization based in New York — seeks an enthusiastic, dedicated, and mission-aligned Director of Data for our After-School, Community, and Early Childhood programs.
The Director of Data Strategy & Performance provides strategic leadership for data governance, performance management, analytics, reporting, and data-informed decision-making across the Deputy Program Officer’s portfolio. Reporting directly to the Deputy Program Officer, the Director establishes the vision, standards, systems, and management routines that enable program leaders to use reliable data to assess performance, identify risks and opportunities, strengthen execution, and improve outcomes for scholars and families.
The Director serves as the senior program-side leader for cross-portfolio data strategy and directly supervises the Assistant Directors of Data. The Director provides formal supervision, performance management, coaching, role expectations, and technical leadership for the Assistant Directors of Data, while Managing Directors maintain a dotted-line relationship to support portfolio alignment, responsiveness, and day-to-day partnership. The Director will partner with organizational teams in IT Evaluation, HR, and other functions to strengthen Salesforce (Zora) usage, data quality and governance, dashboards and scorecards, OKR and core-metric monitoring, and the integration of data into ongoing performance management and strategic planning routines.
The ideal candidate is a strategic and systems-oriented data leader who can set direction, build organizational capacity, lead complex cross-functional initiatives, develop staff, and translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations for senior leadership.
For more information, check out Want to Work at Harlem Children’s Zone? Here’s 7 Things You Need to Know.
