jobs.title: Executive Director, Technology
jobs.text:
About Endpoints News Media Company, LLC
Endpoints News, founded in 2016, is a leading news media company with a clear mission: to deliver the best news product in biopharma and be the essential daily read for industry leaders globally. Now a part of the Financial Times family, Endpoints News has 290,000+ registered readers and continues to grow its reach with breaking news, in-depth analysis, live and virtual events and award-winning journalism.
The Role
This is a leadership role. You lead the technology function across engineering, delivery and operations: setting the standard, making the calls, growing the people, running the work, and answering to the business for what it delivers.
You also ship. The team is small and everyone at Endpoints is an IC at some level, including the people who lead. You'll be in the codebase every week and carrying real work of your own, because that's how things get built here and because it's the only way to lead a team this size credibly.
You'll report to the SVP, Design, Product and Technology and work alongside them daily. A lot of the job is the two of you thinking out loud: what's worth building, what it would take, what it would cost. You'll help shape the technical strategy together (architecture direction, build-versus-buy, where the platform goes next), with the SVP owning the final call and the direction for product and design. The technical thinking is yours, and we'd much rather hear "here's how we could do that" than "here's why we can't".
You'll be the technology counterpart to editorial and commercial leadership. The remit is wider than engineering. Delivery, technical program management, the operational layer, the business systems the company runs on, and the vendors who extend the team all sit with you, and the team beneath you will grow to reflect that.
This role is based in the United States and is fully remote.
What You'll Do
Lead and grow the technology team across engineering, delivery and operations. Own the people side fully — hiring, performance, development and the hard conversations — and manage through a manager as the function scales.
Shape the technical strategy with the SVP — architecture direction, build, buy and integrate calls, and where the platform needs to go next. The SVP owns the final decision; you own the thinking that informs it and the delivery that follows.
Turn product direction into shipped work. Own everything between the outcome, standard and date and working software in production — scoping, technical requirements, sequencing, and the commitments we make back to editorial and business stakeholders.
Run delivery across the technology function. Own the cadence, the dependencies and the visibility that lets the rest of the company know what's coming and when.
Answer for what the team ships. Set the standard, review architecture and overrule it on technical grounds where required, and put mechanisms in place that catch problems before production.
Ship code every week. The team is small and everyone here builds, including the people who lead. You'll carry real work of your own — the hard problems, the spikes that set direction, the things that have to land — alongside the team rather than above it.
Stand up new products and evolve the existing ones across news, subscriptions and identity, data and events, including the wind-down of what the new platform replaces.
Lead security across everything we run: what's exposed, who has access, what's still running that shouldn't be, third-party risk, and the response when something happens.
Own the content and data spine. You and your team build the spine, not the surface: the interface is design's - our designers author the design system and ship it to production themselves. Shape the content model, keep the CMS moving, build the APIs and MCP services every surface and every team draws on, and finish that shift across the rest of the estate.
Own the operational layer — environments, CI, previews, observability, and the road to production that lets a designer ship with confidence.
Own the internal systems and tooling the business runs on — the integrations across CRM, events, email and subscriptions, and the services that let business teams work directly with our own data.
Direct the contractors and vendors who extend the team, and hold their output to the same standard as our own.
Get sound AI-assisted work from non-engineers live quickly, and know when it isn't sound.
Partner with editorial and business leadership to turn ideas into shipped features at the pace a newsroom requires.
Technical Requirements
Our actual stack, not a generic list. We care more about depth than about covering every line.
Hands-on, Every week
TypeScript, Node.js, modern tooling
Payload CMS on PostgreSQL, or equivalent depth in a headless, code-first CMS
Content modeling and API design — GraphQL and REST
Next.js, and Astro with React islands
Application security — authentication and authorization you can demonstrate are enforced, secrets management, dependency hygiene, least privilege
LLM-native workflow — AI tools as a core part of how you and your team build, and knowing where not to use them
Depth you've built before, even where you now direct it
Identity and payments — SSO/OIDC (we run Logto), Stripe, entitlements, paywall logic
AWS — Lambda via OpenNext, S3, CloudFront, IAM, RDS — and containers on Kubernetes
Security operations — attack surface and asset inventory, decommissioning, access lifecycle, credential rotation, logging that can answer a forensic question
Incident response — containment, evidence, and reporting that states what the logs show
Privacy and compliance — GDPR and CCPA, consent and tracking, data retention
PHP, MySQL, Python/FastAPI, Elasticsearch, message brokers
What We're Looking For
A leader first. 5+ years leading technical teams, including managing engineers directly and managing through other managers. You've hired, developed and exited people, set a team's standard, and been accountable for what it delivered.
And a builder every week. Everyone at Endpoints contributes as an IC at some level, and at this team size that includes you. You'll be writing and shipping production code regularly, not symbolically.
Leadership beyond engineering. You've owned delivery, operations, vendor relationships and stakeholder commitments — not just the codebase — and you've been the person the business holds to account for technology outcomes.
And a builder every week. Everyone at Endpoints contributes as an IC at some level, and at this team size that includes you. You'll be writing and shipping production code regularly, not symbolically.
You take a short ask and build the right thing. A sentence of business intent is enough for you to come back with what it means technically, what it costs and what it breaks.
Real backend and infrastructure depth, even where you no longer use it daily. You'll be accountable for work you don't write.
You've worked where designers ship their own code.
You've directed contractors and vendors and held their output to your own standard.
A thinking partner. The SVP will bring you ideas and expect a real conversation: what it would take, what it would break, and what a better version might be. You make your case, and you commit once the call is made.
Comfortable being the technical voice in a room of editorial and commercial leaders, and translating in both directions.
A background in media or publishing is a strong plus, not a requirement.
Compensation
Total compensation opportunity: ~$215,000, inclusive of ~$175k base and ~$40k annual bonus.
It's important to note that salary information provided in job descriptions is subject to change and may be dependent on a variety of factors such as location, experience, and qualifications. The salary range provided is meant to give potential applicants an idea of the compensation they can expect, but it is not a guarantee of a specific salary. Actual salary may vary based on individual factors and negotiations. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate based on salary history or other personal factors.
Why Join Us?
🌍 Work From Anywhere!
👥 Positive, Supportive, and Collaborative Work Culture.
🌴 Paid Time Off: Generous PTO is offered annually, plus 12 company holidays and 2 floating holidays!
🩺Medical Insurance: Endpoints pays 70% of premiums for employee, spouse, and/or dependents.
🦷Fully-Paid Benefits for Employees: Dental and Vision insurance, Short-Term and Long Term Disability, $50,000 Basic Life and AD&D Insurance, and our Employee Assistance Program.
📁 Additional Life, Hospital, Critical Illness, and Accident Insurance: Offered through Guardian.
🩹 MDLIVE: See a doctor, mental health professional, nutritionist, or dermatologist on your time and online!
👪 Family Leave: All employees are eligible for fully-paid Primary or Secondary Caregiver Leave for the birth or adoption of a child.
💪 Paid Volunteer Days: Provides employees with the opportunity to engage in community service & volunteer activities.
💸 401K: Endpoints will match 100% of the first 3% of an employee's contribution; followed by 50% match of the next 2%.
💻 Equipment Provided: Laptop, monitor, and additional equipment needs.
📱WFH Stipend: $75 per month to cover the costs of working from home.
🏠 Home Office Stipend: $500 annually to help you create your dream office.
💊 Benefits Marketplace: We’ve partnered with Bennie to provide discounted products for employees such as other insurances, family planning & support, behavioral health, wellness, pet insurance, and financial wellness.
💼 MetLife Legal: We’ve partnered with MetLife Legal Services to provide a discounted legal plan for our employees.
Endpoints News is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diverse backgrounds and thoughts and welcome everyone to apply for employment with us. We are committed to fostering an environment that is inclusive, transparent, and collaborative. Mutual respect is central to how Endpoints News operates, and we believe the best solutions come from diverse perspectives, experiences, and skills. We embrace our differences and know that we are stronger working together.

jobs.title: Head of Engineering, NIRA
jobs.text:
Join the Tilt team
At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. Our mobile-first products and machine learning-powered credit models look beyond credit scores, using over 250 real-time financial signals to recognize real potential. With millions of customers worldwide, we're not just changing how people access financial products — we're creating a new credit system that backs the working, whatever they're working toward.
The Opportunity: Senior Engineering Manager, Nira
We’re looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead our NIRA team, owning engineering across product, platform reliability, data infrastructure, and internal tooling. This is a high-impact role where you’ll work closely with Product, Data Science, Credit, and Marketing to build, scale, and improve a fast-growing business.
Location: Bengaluru, India (Hybrid)
How you'll make an impact
Own and execute the engineering roadmap across NIRA
Raise the bar on engineering practices (CI/CD, testing, reliability, observability)
Lead and grow a high-performing team of engineers
Drive technical decisions that balance speed, quality, and scalability
Partner cross-functionally to deliver meaningful business outcomes
Why you're a great fit
7+ years in engineering, with 3+ years in management
Experience leading teams in startup or scaling environments
Strong track record improving engineering standards and delivery
Comfortable operating across product, infrastructure, and data
Clear communicator with a bias for action
Our Interview Process
Initial Recruiter Call: A conversation to learn about your experience and what you're looking for in your next role.
Hiring Manager Interview: A deeper discussion about your experience.
Skills Panel: Meet with Tilt team members to discuss your expertise and problem-solving approach.
Leadership Conversation: A final conversation with a leader to discuss how you'll contribute to Tilt's mission, and how we can help you achieve your career goals along the way.
Don’t meet every qualification? We care about potential over your past. If you're bringing ambition and drive to what we're building, we want to hear from you.
What you'll get at Tilt
Virtual-first teamwork: The Tilt team is collaborating across 14 countries, 12 time zones, and counting. You’ll get started with a WFH office reimbursement.
Competitive pay: We're big on potential, and it's reflected in our competitive compensation packages and generous equity.
Complete support: Find flexible health plans at every premium level, and substantial subsidies that stand up to global standards.
Visibility is yours: You can count on direct exposure to our leadership team — we’re a team where good ideas travel quickly.
Paid global onsites: Magic happens IRL: we gather twice yearly to reconnect over shared meals or kayaking adventures. (We’ve visited Vail, San Diego, and Mexico City, to name a few.)
Impact is recognized: Growth opportunities follow your contributions, not rigid promotion timelines.
The Tilt Way
We're looking for people who chase excellence and impact. Those who stand behind their work, celebrating the wins and learning from the missteps equally. We foster an environment where every voice is valued and mutual respect is non-negotiable — brilliant jerks need not apply. We're in this together, working to expand access to fair credit and prove that people are incredible. When you join us, it's not just another day at the [virtual] office, you're helping millions of hardworking people reach better financial futures.
You’re pushing ahead in your career? We can get behind that. Join us in building the credit system that people deserve.

jobs.text:
ABOUT TIDE
At Tide, we help SMEs save time and money in the running of their businesses by not only offering business accounts and related banking services, but also a comprehensive set of highly usable and connected administrative solutions, from invoicing to accounting.
Tide is transforming the small business banking market and now supports over 2 million members globally across the UK, India, Germany and France.
Using advanced technology, all solutions are designed with SMEs in mind. With quick onboarding, low fees and innovative features, we thrive on making data driven decisions to serve our mission: to help SMEs save time and money so they can get back to doing what they love.
Tide facts:
Tide is available for UK, Indian, German and French SMEs
Over 2 million members globally and rapidly growing
Over $300 million raised in funding
3,000 Tideans globally
Recognised with Great Place to Work certification three years in a row, and among India’s Top 50 Best Workplaces in Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance in 2026
We have offices in Central London, with a member support and technology centre in Sofia, Bulgaria, technology centres in Serbia, Romania, Lithuania and Hyderabad and offices in Gurugram, New Delhi, Berlin, Paris and Luxembourg
ABOUT THE TEAM:
PCS helps small businesses find and take the right credit. The Credit Outcome vertical is the heaviest part of PCS: it owns the journey from a business's intent to a successful credit outcome, measured by our north-star metric, % 1st Outcome. It spans several markets and combines market-focused product teams (Scaled Markets, New Markets, India) with horizontal teams (Sales Engine and Platform). You will work hand in hand with a dedicated Engineering Director, Design, Product Operations, Analytics and Commercial Heads.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
Vision, strategy and outcomes
Own the vertical's north star: set the strategy and roadmap to grow % 1st Outcome, balancing margin, efficiency and member experience.
Place the big bets: prioritise across routing, human connection, integrations and decisioning (e.g. pre-qualification), and be explicit about what we will not do.
Regional focus: make sound trade-offs between markets, including scaling established markets and building new ones such as India.
Leadership and team growth
Lead and grow product leaders: hire, coach and develop Product Leads and Senior PMs, giving each a self-contained area of the business to own.
Clear ownership: ensure one accountable PM/EM pair per workstream, with no ambiguity on who owns what.
Operating rhythm: run planning, OKRs and reviews that connect team work to vertical and company goals.
Partnership and delivery
Engineering partnership: work as a true pair with the Engineering Director on roadmap, capacity and technical investment, including platform health.
Cross-functional influence: align Design, Data, Risk & Compliance, Commercial and Operations on priorities and launches.
Data and experimentation: use funnel analytics and experiments to find friction, make decisions and show impact in commercial terms.
Applied AI: identify where automation and AI (e.g. lead scoring, agentic sales tooling) can raise conversion and efficiency.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR:
Experience: 8+ years in product management, with 3+ years leading product managers or product leads [TBC level/years].
Commercial acumen: you tie product decisions to revenue, margin and unit economics.
Data-native: comfortable with funnel analytics, experimentation and BI tools.
Technical fluency: you can engage confidently with engineers on APIs, integrations and data flows.
Leader of leaders: you coach strong PMs, set a high bar and create room for people to grow.
Influence without authority: you align senior stakeholders across functions and regions.
Nice to have: experience in lending, credit marketplaces, fintech or regulated financial services; experience building products in multiple markets, ideally including India.
WHAT YOU’LL GET IN RETURN:
Competitive Compensation - competitive salary and share options
Time Off – Generous annual leave on top of bank holidays.
Parental Leave – Paid maternity, paternity, and adoption leave to support your family journey.
Sabbatical – Extended unpaid and paid leave options after completing milestone years with Tide.
Health Insurance – Private family insurance with additional OPD coverage and top-up options.
Life & Accident Cover – Comprehensive accidental and life insurance protection.
Mental Wellbeing – Access to therapy sessions, courses, meditations, and workshops.
Volunteering & Development Days – Paid days annually for volunteering or personal growth.
Learning & Development – Annual budget for books, courses, coaching, and more.
WOO (Work Outside the Office) – Work from abroad for up to 90 days annually.
Home Office Setup – Contribution towards setting up your home office
Laptop Ownership – Keep your old laptop and get a new one when it’s time for a replacement.
Snacks & Meals – Office perks with snacks, coffee, tea, and lunch (location dependent).
TIDE IS A PLACE FOR EVERYONE
At Tide, we believe that we can only succeed if we let our differences enrich our culture. Our Tideans come from a variety of backgrounds and experience levels. We consider everyone irrespective of their ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran, neurodiversity or differently-abled status. We celebrate diversity in our workforce as a cornerstone of our success. Our commitment to a broad spectrum of ideas and backgrounds is what enables us to build products that resonate with our members’ diverse needs and lives.
We are One Team and foster a transparent and inclusive environment, where everyone’s voice is heard.
At Tide, we thrive on diversity, embracing various backgrounds and experiences. We welcome all individuals regardless of ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability. Our inclusive culture is key to our success, helping us build products that meet our members' diverse needs. We are One Team, committed to transparency and ensuring everyone’s voice is heard.

Tide does not charge any fees at any stage of the recruitment process.
All official Tide job opportunities are listed exclusively on our Careers Page and applications should be submitted through this channel.
Communication from Tide will only come from an official @tide.co email address.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Enterprise Data Governance
jobs.text:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.
General Description:
BeOne is seeking an Associate Director, Enterprise Data Governance to build, enable, and scale enterprise data governance and stewardship capabilities across the organization. This role is a key member of the Enterprise Data Governance function and is responsible for operationalizing data stewardship within a federated governance model.
Working closely with the Head of Enterprise Data Governance, this position will serve as a subject matter expert (SME), translating governance strategy, policy, and regulatory requirements into practical, scalable business processes. The Associate Director will lead domain onboarding, drive stewardship adoption, and oversee strategic governance initiatives.
This role partners across business, technology, security, privacy, legal, and compliance teams to establish trusted, compliant, and well-governed data assets that support analytics, AI readiness, regulatory compliance, and business decision-making. The position will also provide leadership to managed service providers and junior governance resources while monitoring stewardship effectiveness through defined metrics and reporting.
Essential Functions of the Job:
Serve as a SME for enterprise data governance and data stewardship, contributing to governance operating models, policies, standards, processes, and best practices.
Lead onboarding of business and data domains into the federated governance framework, including role enablement, stewardship adoption, and governance process implementation.
Enable enterprise data discovery, transparency, and reuse through metadata management, data catalog, and data marketplace capabilities.
Implement metadata management, business glossary curation, and stewardship workflows.
Integrate governance processes across enterprise platforms and business workflows.
Influence the adoption of governance and stewardship practices without direct authority by building trusted relationships and aligning stakeholders around shared objectives.
Leverage automation and AI-enabled capabilities to improve stewardship efficiency and governance effectiveness.
Establish, monitor, and report governance KPIs, initiative progress, stewardship outcomes, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
Partner with platform owners, architects, and data teams to ensure governance technologies effectively support stewardship, metadata management, data quality, and compliance requirements.
Author governance policies, standards, procedures, and operating models aligned with enterprise data management best practices.
Lead stakeholder engagement sessions, governance working groups, and training programs that drive accountability, stewardship, and sustained adoption.
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree and 8+ years of experience in data governance, data stewardship, enterprise data management, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated experience serving as a data governance SME within a federated, matrixed, or enterprise-scale operating model.
Proven ability to influence outcomes and drive adoption of governance processes, standards, and platforms without formal authority.
Experience leading cross-functional governance initiatives involving business, technology, and compliance stakeholders.
Hands-on experience implementing and driving adoption of enterprise data governance platforms such as Informatica, Atlan, Alation, or similar solutions.
Experience enabling and training data stewards, data owners, and business stakeholders on governance processes and tools.
Experience with data classification, metadata management, data quality, and regulatory-aligned governance practices.
Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to navigate competing priorities across business and technology organizations.
Experience leading, mentoring, or coordinating team members, managed service providers, or governance resources.
Demonstrated ability to translate governance strategy, policy, and regulatory requirements into practical, scalable operating processes.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience leading governance platform implementations and stewardship adoption initiatives (Informatica, Atlan, Collibra, Alation, etc…).
Strong facilitation skills, including governance workshops, onboarding sessions, and working groups.
Experience supporting Data-as-a-Product operating models on modern data platforms such as Databricks and Snowflake.
Experience governing data within regulated environments, including GxP, clinical, R&D, or pharmaceutical domains.
Experience defining and reporting governance and stewardship KPIs to senior leadership.
Understanding of how metadata, stewardship, and data quality capabilities enable analytics, AI, and business outcomes.
Relevant certifications such as CDMP, DGSP, DCAM, DAMA, or equivalent credentials.
Supervisory Responsibilities:
Supervisory responsibilities are delivery-focused and include leading and providing direction for our managed service providers on certain projects, while providing strategic oversight and direction to junior data governance resources.
Global Competencies
When we exhibit our values of Patients First, Driving Excellence, Bold Ingenuity and Collaborative Spirit, through our twelve global competencies below, we help get more affordable medicines to more patients around the world.
Fosters Teamwork
Provides and Solicits Honest and Actionable Feedback
Self-Awareness
Acts Inclusively
Demonstrates Initiative
Entrepreneurial Mindset
Continuous Learning
Embraces Change
Results-Oriented
Analytical Thinking/Data Analysis
Financial Excellence
Communicates with Clarity
Salary Range: $143,700.00 - $193,700.00 annually
BeOne is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Actual compensation packages are determined by several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, depth of experience, certifications, relevant education or training, and specific work location. Packages may vary by location due to differences in the cost of labor. The recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for a preferred location during the hiring process. Please note that the listed range reflects the base salary or hourly range only. Non-Commercial roles are eligible to participate in the annual bonus plan, and Commercial roles are eligible to participate in an incentive compensation plan. All Company employees have the opportunity to own shares of BeOne Medicines Ltd. stock because all employees are eligible for discretionary equity awards and to voluntarily participate in the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The Company has a comprehensive benefits package that includes Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), FSA/HSA, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, and Wellness.
We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. BeOne does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, national origin, veteran status or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. In order to ensure reasonable accommodation for individuals protected by Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, and any other applicable federal, state or local laws, applicants who require reasonable accommodation in the job application process may contact .

jobs.title: SVP, Product
jobs.text:
About Toptal
Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.
We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.
Position Description:
As SVP, Product, you will shape the vision as to where Toptal’s products and platforms go next and then drive the execution to build them. This is the most senior product role in the company. You will report to the Chief Executive Officer, sit on the executive team, and work collaboratively with our Engineering, Design, Finance, Marketing, New Businesses, Professional Services, and Customer leaders. AI is not a line item on your roadmap. It is the roadmap.
You should be Toptal’s foremost expert on what AI means for products and platforms. That means real depth in fine-tuning and post-training, agent design and evaluation, and the economics of running models in production, along with the judgment to know which applies to us. Work directly with our AI researchers rather than through them. We expect both the AI agenda and the product strategy to originate with you. We will react to your plan rather than hand you ours.
This is a hands-on role. You will write your own specs and pull your own data. When you think an agent could take over a piece of work, you will build a rough version and find out whether it holds up before anyone budgets for it. You will sit in product reviews and say what you actually think. We move fast, and we need Product setting the pace. You will own and set the standards for the hiring bar for the product team, bringing in talent that will advance Toptal to the next level.
Your remit runs across the business: the core platform, the talent and client experiences, the internal systems that run it, the products we take to market, and the data and AI platform underneath them. You will work hand in hand with Engineering on the platform all of it runs on, fold acquisitions and new products into the portfolio, and know growth marketing cold, because how a product reaches the market is part of building it.
Product is yours to shape at blazing speed: scoping, sizing the teams, planning headcount, and defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing them off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about landing an A player and treats an open seat as urgent. Your own dedication and hard work will set the tone, and the people you bring in should be inspired to do the best work of their careers on this team. We are looking for the person who will define what an AI-native product organization looks like and then run it successfully.
This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.
Responsibilities:
The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.
AI and agentic product
Own Toptal’s AI product strategy: where agents and models belong across the marketplace, the talent and client experiences, our internal systems, and the products we take to market, along with the business outcomes they carry.
Decide what we build with AI and what we do not, including build-versus-buy on models and tooling and the packaging and pricing of AI-enabled products.
Make AI quality measurable through evals, acceptance bars, and review loops, and partner with Engineering on the platform as its most demanding customer.
Rebuild how Product works using AI, raising the output and judgment of every product manager through AI-assisted discovery, research, prototyping, and analysis. Product managers have to want this rather than comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.
Portfolio and operating model
Own the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for the whole portfolio: what we build, what we sunset, and how investment is distributed across growth, platform, and operational leverage.
Establish the product operating model and the metrics behind it, so decisions are made on evidence and user research rather than opinion.
Own the product integration of acquisitions and new products, and act as a senior voice of the customer for both talent and clients.
Team and accountability
Decide what a product team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.
Own resourcing and workforce planning, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.
Review the product work directly, develop people against a clear bar, and raise it as the organization grows.
In the first week, expect to:
Work to get up to speed with how the organization runs, including how our operational frameworks work.
Begin building relationships with the CEO, the executive team, and your direct reports.
Begin learning Toptal’s platform architecture, marketplace dynamics, internal tooling, and current AI initiatives and capabilities.
In the first month, expect to:
Assess the current state of the Product organization and its AI maturity: its people, its roadmap, its rituals, and where the gaps are, including the team against the bar this role requires.
Bring the executive team a product strategy no one asked you for.
Become acquainted with the full product portfolio, the company’s goals, and those you will partner with.
Establish a shared view with the CEO and the executive team of the company’s priorities and how product supports them.
Start collaborating closely with your product teams.
In the first three months, expect to:
Own the product portfolio, its strategy, and its roadmap, and be executing your own plan with at least one AI-enabled capability already in production and measured.
Present your resourcing plan and a clear point of view to the executive team on where product investment should concentrate, what should be deprioritized, and why.
Establish or refine the product operating model: planning cadence, prioritization framework, and the metrics the organization will be held to, with the trust of the peers and teams you work with most closely.
In the first six months, expect to:
Show business impact from AI-enabled products in at least two core surfaces, with the evidence behind it, and visible progress against the top portfolio priorities measured against the metrics you defined.
Have the right leadership team in place, with a clear plan to close any remaining gaps.
Be inspiring and mentoring the teams you work with, upleveling how the organization brainstorms, collaborates, and executes, and charting a clear path for scaling Product’s impact.
In the first year, expect to:
Run a product organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with AI leverage embedded in the portfolio and the operating model rather than living in a set of pilots.
Have built an exceptional product team doing the best work of their careers, with a record of building impactful products in a timely and elegant fashion.
Deliver on your roadmap priorities and promises, with a demonstrable link between product investment and business results, and Product established as a trusted, high-leverage function that the rest of the company plans around.
Qualifications and Job Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree is required, preferably in a technical discipline (Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems). Masters is strongly preferred.
At least 15 years of proven software Product Management experience.
At least 8 years of experience leading Product organizations, including experience leading other product leaders (managing managers).
Proven ability to raise the level of a product organization through the people you hire and develop.
Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, with a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.
Experience owning an entire product portfolio at a high-growth technology company, with accountability for business outcomes and not solely delivery.
Demonstrated success setting product strategy at the executive level and translating it into an executable roadmap across multiple teams and domains.
Experience leading AI-enabled products, with a focus on delivering measurable business outcomes.
Deep, hands-on command of modern AI as a product discipline: agentic architectures, harness and orchestration design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation, along with the economics of running models in production. You have shipped these yourself.
Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.

As SVP, Product, you will shape the vision as to where Toptal’s products and platforms go next and then drive the execution to build them. This is the most senior product role in the company. You will report to the Chief Executive Officer, sit on the executive team, and work collaboratively with our Engineering, Design, Finance, Marketing, New Businesses, Professional Services, and Customer leaders. AI is not a line item on your roadmap. It is the roadmap.

You should be Toptal’s foremost expert on what AI means for products and platforms. That means real depth in fine-tuning and post-training, agent design and evaluation, and the economics of running models in production, along with the judgment to know which applies to us. Work directly with our AI researchers rather than through them. We expect both the AI agenda and the product strategy to originate with you. We will react to your plan rather than hand you ours.

This is a hands-on role. You will write your own specs and pull your own data. When you think an agent could take over a piece of work, you will build a rough version and find out whether it holds up before anyone budgets for it. You will sit in product reviews and say what you actually think. We move fast, and we need Product setting the pace. You will own and set the standards for the hiring bar for the product team, bringing in talent that will advance Toptal to the next level.

Your remit runs across the business: the core platform, the talent and client experiences, the internal systems that run it, the products we take to market, and the data and AI platform underneath them. You will work hand in hand with Engineering on the platform all of it runs on, fold acquisitions and new products into the portfolio, and know growth marketing cold, because how a product reaches the market is part of building it.

Product is yours to shape at blazing speed: scoping, sizing the teams, planning headcount, and defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing them off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about landing an A player and treats an open seat as urgent. Your own dedication and hard work will set the tone, and the people you bring in should be inspired to do the best work of their careers on this team. We are looking for the person who will define what an AI-native product organization looks like and then run it successfully.

Make AI quality measurable through evals, acceptance bars, and review loops, and partner with Engineering on the platform as its most demanding customer.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.text:
About Toptal
Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.
We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.
Position Description:
As Chief Technology Officer, you will drive execution for the product and engineering teams and put AI at the core of everything the company builds. You will own Toptal’s full technical architecture and you will build it AI-first—utilizing best practices for agentic engineering. AI is not a workstream inside the engineer team—its core to it.
You will create and own the AI architecture and best practices the rest of the company utilizes. You will also own the initiatives that put agents into production. You should know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up, how to engineer best-in-class harnesses, and how to create best practices for agentic engineering that engineering teams adopt to 10x their productivity—without sacrificing quality. Your mindset will be that of a builder and an architect, someone who solves problems in the system itself. No problem will be too large or too small for you to solve yourself. You will set the technical direction and hold the cadenced meetings that turns technical strategy into working, production-ready outcomes. You will be in the design reviews and in the code, not adjacent to them. You will move fast, and you will ensure our engineering team is never the reason an initiative slows down.
You are the technical owner of all Toptal’s products. You will collaborate closely with Product to design infrastructure that exposes Toptal’s core business logic through modular interfaces the rest of the business can build on. Alongside a group of hands-on executives, your engineering discipline directly shapes Toptal’s growth, profitability, and operational excellence.
You will own resourcing and workforce planning as a doer: scoping the work, sizing the teams, planning headcount against it, defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing it off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about hiring A-players—with a sense of urgency.
Then, you lead the team. You will set the standards, develop people against those standards, and know exactly who is meeting those standards.
You will be one of Toptal’s foremost experts on AI, and you will stay ahead of a field that never stops moving. You will coach engineers on agentic best practices, show the executive team what is newly possible with the new AI tooling, and push AI into every function at Toptal.
This role runs on high-energy execution and attention to detail. You will bring urgency to every part of it and measure yourself on outcomes. We are not looking for someone to oversee this work. We are looking for someone to drive it and get into the detiwls.
This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.
Responsibilities:
The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.
One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction.
AI and agentic engineering
Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against.
Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for.
Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed.
Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.
Team, resourcing, and accountability
Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.
Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.
Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows.
Platform and execution
Own the architecture end to end, from services and data flows to interfaces and system boundaries, and hold the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.
Own throughput, reliability, and the platform layer beneath them, including the AI-dependent paths where latency, drift, and provider outages are real failure modes. Own build-versus-buy, technical debt, secure-by-design architecture, responsible AI, and the engineering and AI cost structure down to inference and token spend.
In the first week, expect to:
Learn Toptal’s model and platform architecture, and meet the leaders you will depend on across Engineering, Product, Industries, and Services.
Establish a direct, working rhythm with the CEO.
In the first month, expect to:
Assess the engineering function honestly, and assess AI maturity with it: what is really in production, what is measured, what is duplicated, and what should be shut down.
Assess the team against the bar this role requires, and bring the executive team a strategy no one asked you for.
In the first three months, expect to:
Be executing your own plan, with a review cadence and clear accountability at every level, and your resourcing plan presented.
Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result.
In the first six months, expect to:
Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it.
Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most.
In the first year, expect to:
Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering.
Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan.
Qualifications and Job Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale.
Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up.
Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work.
Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence.
Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers.
Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.
You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI.
Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.
Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale.
Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield.
Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself.
You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.
Compensation

jobs.title: Vice President, Product Management (MDR)
jobs.text:
Vice President, Product Management (MDR)
Rapid7 is looking for a Vice President, Product Management to own the strategy, vision, and execution of our Managed Detection & Response (MDR) product portfolio. This is a rare opportunity to shape how thousands of organizations experience cybersecurity as a managed service, defining what great looks like at the intersection of human expertise and cutting-edge technology.
About the Team
Rapid7's MDR product team partners closely with our SOC, engineering, and go-to-market functions to shape the service experience, define platform capabilities, and continuously raise the bar on global managed security service delivery.
About the Role
As a Vice President, Product Management (MDR), your primary responsibility will be to set the product direction for Rapid7's managed security service while balancing customer needs, analyst capabilities, and strategic business goals. Specifically, your focus will be to:
Define and drive the MDR product strategy and roadmap, ensuring alignment with Rapid7's broader detection and response vision
Partner closely with SOC leadership to deeply understand analyst workflows, operational pain points, and necessary platform capabilities
Lead and develop a high-performing team of product managers, fostering accountability and continuous learning
Translate customer insights, market trends, and competitive intelligence into differentiated product decisions that drive retention and expansion
Collaborate with engineering to define and deliver a platform roadmap that gives MDR analysts speed, context, and automation
Serve as a senior customer-facing voice for the MDR product by engaging with strategic accounts and building trust through transparency
Define and track product OKRs and success metrics to continuously improve the service experience and business outcomes
Work cross-functionally with sales, marketing, and customer success to ensure product positioning, launch readiness, and customer adoption
The skills and qualities you'll bring include
Bring 12+ years of product management experience, with significant time spent leading product for managed services, SaaS platforms, or security products
Possess a deep understanding of the cybersecurity landscape, particularly in detection and response, MDR, SOC operations, or incident response
Demonstrate a proven track record of leading and scaling product teams in a fast-paced, customer-centric environment
Drive multi-year product vision through strategic doing while staying grounded in near-term execution and time-bound milestones
Establish clear accountability and ownership across teams to deliver value for managed service customers
Make efficient decisions that resolve complex product challenges and maintain operational momentum across functions
Communicate complex product strategies clearly to executive and customer audiences to foster commitment
Build global cross-functional networks across engineering, services, sales, and executive leadership to drive aligned business outcomes
Embrace challenging conversations constructively to find common ground across cross-functional stakeholder groups
Apply self-awareness to adapt leadership style to varying group dynamics across technical and business teams
Demonstrate an eager mindset toward navigating change by driving product evolution in a fast-moving market
Embody our core values to foster a culture of excellence that drives meaningful impact and collective success.
We know that the best ideas and solutions come from multi-dimensional teams. That’s because these teams reflect a variety of backgrounds and professional experiences. If you are excited about this role and feel your experience can make an impact, please don’t be shy - apply today.
About Rapid7
At Rapid7, our vision is to create a secure digital world for our customers, our industry, and our communities. We do this by harnessing our collective expertise and passion to challenge what’s possible and drive extraordinary impact. jobs.title: Sr. Director, Technology Program Management
jobs.text:
FICO (NYSE: FICO)is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential!
The Opportunity
FICO’s Global PMO is the function that keeps the company’s most critical enterprise programs on track, from strategic transformation initiatives to cross-functional platform investments. As Sr. Director, Technology Program Management, a senior leadership role within our Project Management discipline, you will build and lead the PMO’s technology program portfolio, ensuring critical initiatives land with speed, discipline, and measurable outcomes. This role reports into the VP of the Global PMO. The flagship program under this role is FICO’s Product and Engineering Transformation, moving the engineering organization to AI-native, service-oriented delivery at scale. In this new role, you’ll lead strategic oversight and portfolio governance while building the function alongside technology and product executives.
What You’ll Contribute
Own the Global PMO technology program portfolio, ensuring well-orchestrated delivery of key roadmap initiatives, establishing effective governance and prioritization frameworks, and bringing a predictable reporting cadence that gives leadership clear visibility into program health, risk, and investment performance across all active initiatives.
Serve as the executive escalation point for program-level decisions and cross-program conflicts, and champion AI-native, agile-at-scale program delivery by creating and evolving PMO methodologies, templates, and tooling, reducing ceremony and modeling the operating principles FICO is embedding across its engineering organization.
Provide senior sponsorship and strategic oversight for FICO’s flagship Product and Engineering Transformation program, rolling up the sleeves on implementation and partnering with executive sponsors across Product, Engineering, HR, Legal, and Security to align direction and resolve blockers requiring SVP-level engagement.
Hold the AI transformation team accountable to milestones, quality, and stakeholder outcomes, and represent program progress and risks in executive forums, translating complexity into clear business impact.
Act as a trusted partner to the Head of Product, Head of Engineering and Architecture, Head of Technology Operations, and other technology executives, providing the portfolio-level view needed to make investment and resourcing decisions.
Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing team of program managers, defining career paths, competency frameworks, and performance standards, while building a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement that earns the trust of engineering and product teams rather than adding bureaucratic overhead.
Drive and improve annual and quarterly technology program planning cycles, owning portfolio-level dashboards and executive reporting as the trusted source of truth on status, investment tracking, and outcomes.
Identify cross-program synergies, shared infrastructure needs, and resourcing conflicts early, and partner with Finance and HR to manage program budgets, headcount plans, and vendor relationships across the portfolio.
What We’re Seeking
Extensive, progressive experience in program and portfolio management specifically in product and engineering disciplines, including senior leadership experience overseeing technology programs in a complex enterprise environment.
Prior firsthand involvement in implementing and scaling AI-native or Agentic delivery frameworks and tooling.
Demonstrated success leading large-scale organizational and technology transformation programs, with a clear understanding of what enables them to succeed and what causes them to fail.
Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to engage credibly with senior leadership, translate complexity into business impact, and influence without authority across a matrixed organization.
Experience building and leading high-performing PMO or program management teams, including hiring, developing, and retaining senior individual contributors and managers.
Deep understanding of software product and engineering organizations, including what slows delivery down and what governance models enable rather than impede progress.
Track record of building portfolio governance models that provide real oversight without adding bureaucratic drag.
Experience managing programs at the intersection of technology, organizational change, and business strategy simultaneously.
Familiarity with modern software delivery practices such as CI/CD, DevOps, and agile at scale is preferred, enabling credible assessment of program risk and engagement with engineering leaders.
Our Offer to You
An inclusive culture strongly reflecting our core values: Act Like an Owner, Delight Our Customers and Earn the Respect of Others.
The opportunity to make an impact and develop professionally by leveraging your unique strengths and participating in valuable learning experiences.
Highly competitive compensation, benefits and rewards programs that encourage you to bring your best every day and be recognized for doing so.
An engaging, people-first work environment offering work/life balance, employee resource groups, and social events to promote interaction and camaraderie.
The targeted base pay range for this role is: $150,500 to $236,500 with this range reflecting differences in candidate knowledge, skills and experience.
Why Make a Move to FICO?
At FICO, you can develop your career with a leading organization in one of the fastest-growing fields in technology today – Big Data analytics. You’ll play a part in our commitment to help businesses use data to improve every choice they make, using advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning, optimization, and much more.
FICO makes a real difference in the way businesses operate worldwide:
• Credit Scoring — FICO® Scores are used by 90 of the top 100 US lenders.
• Fraud Detection and Security — 4 billion payment cards globally are protected by FICO fraud systems.
• Lending — 3/4 of US mortgages are approved using the FICO Score.
Global trends toward digital transformation have created tremendous demand for FICO’s solutions, placing us among the world’s top 100 software companies by revenue. We help many of the world’s largest banks, insurers, retailers, telecommunications providers and other firms reach a new level of success. Our success is dependent on really talented people – just like you – who thrive on the collaboration and innovation that’s nurtured by a diverse and inclusive environment. We’ll provide the support you need, while ensuring you have the freedom to develop your skills and grow your career. Join FICO and help change the way business thinks!
Learn more about how you can fulfil your potential at
FICO promotes a culture of inclusion and seeks to attract a diverse set of candidates for each job opportunity. We are an equal employment opportunity employer and we’re proud to offer employment and advancement opportunities to all candidates without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. Research has shown that women and candidates from underrepresented communities may not apply for an opportunity if they don’t meet all stated qualifications. While our qualifications are clearly related to role success, each candidate’s profile is unique and strengths in certain skill and/or experience areas can be equally effective. If you believe you have many, but not necessarily all, of the stated qualifications we encourage you to apply.

jobs.text:
(GAQ427R231)
About the role
As Databricks scales at unprecedented velocity, how we invest our R&D capital—both human and compute—is critical to our scale. We are looking for a Product Finance leader to own R&D capital allocation and engineering operations. You will be a key finance partner to our senior Engineering and Product Operations leaders, with a mandate that spans product-level R&D ROI, global workforce and location strategy, and the rapidly evolving economics of AI-enabled software development.
The impact you will have
Drive product-level ROI and R&D capital allocation
Establish frameworks to measure product-level ROI across a fast-moving platform like Databricks where engineering velocity is extremely high.
Operationalize ROI metrics so they directly inform product investment and resource allocation decisions.
Define engineering economics in the AI era
Partner with Engineering to model how AI developer tooling and internal token spend scale alongside headcount, quantifying the tradeoff between human capital and compute capital.
Measure the end-to-end cost of AI-enabled engineering, including the second-order impact on cloud spend, and partner with Engineering to optimize investments.
Shape global workforce and location strategy
Drive multi-year headcount planning across global engineering hubs, balancing cost per hire, talent density, and university recruiting pipelines.
Partner closely with Workplace and Facilities leadership to synchronize R&D hiring roadmaps with global real estate strategy and multi-year CapEx planning.
Scale R&D finance operations and build the team
Bring systems-level thinking to R&D finance operations, building scalable, automated workflows across headcount management, PO planning, monthly accruals, and SOX audit compliance.
Dogfood the Databricks platform to modernize internal finance tooling and deliver self-serve operational visibility to engineering leaders.
Build, mentor, and scale a high-performing team of finance professionals capable of operating seamlessly across strategic capital allocation and rigorous operational execution.
What we look for
Required
10+ years of experience in Strategic/Product Finance or R&D FP&A.
Deep experience managing large-scale R&D OpEx, headcount capacity modeling, and multi-site workforce planning within a high-growth enterprise software or cloud company.
A proven track record of partnering directly with senior Engineering, Product Operations, and People/Workplace executives to drive capital allocation and operational rigor.
Systems-level thinker with a demonstrated ability to re-engineer financial processes from scratch—spanning headcount tracking, procurement, close, and SOX controls—to support rapid scale.
Experience building, leading, and developing high-output finance teams in fast-moving environments.
Preferred
Direct experience analyzing cloud dev/test infrastructure and AI tooling/token costs.
Experience attributing shared engineering and platform R&D costs across a complex, multi-product portfolio to establish product-level profitability.
Hands-on proficiency with SQL, Python, or notebook environments (especially Databricks) to automate reporting and self-serve insights from large operational datasets.

jobs.title: National Council for Mental Wellbeing Director, Learning Technology
jobs.text:
About the National Council for Mental Wellbeing
The vision of the National Council for Mental Wellbeing is to make mental wellbeing, including recovery from substance use challenges, a reality for everyone. Despite overwhelming need, nearly 30 million people across the U.S. do not have access to comprehensive mental health and substance use treatment.
Founded in 1969, the National Council is a 501(c)(3) membership organization that drives policy and social change on behalf of more than 3,100 mental health and substance use treatment organizations and the more than 10 million children, adults and families they serve. We advocate for policies to ensure equitable access to high-quality services, build the capacity of mental health and substance use treatment organizations, and promote greater understanding of mental wellbeing as a core component of health and health care. Through Mental Health First Aid (MHFA), we have trained more than 4.5 million people in the U.S. to identify, understand and respond to signs and symptoms of mental health and substance use challenges.
The National Council operates as a remote-first organization, with employees working from locations across the United States.
The Opportunity
As Director, Learning Technology, you will help the National Council expand and improve its learning offerings by translating learner needs and program priorities into effective technology solutions. You will lead the continued development of an established learning technology ecosystem, including a custom-built platform, and help shape what it can do next. The opportunity is to understand the problems learners and program teams need to solve, explore the technical possibilities and guide the development of capabilities that make a meaningful difference.
From the start, you will work with product, program and learning colleagues to understand how the platform is used, where learners and teams encounter challenges, and what new use cases require. You will get to know its architecture, integrations and workflows, translate needs into functional specifications, and work with developers and vendors to carry improvements from design through testing and release. The product and program teams provide the business needs for the National Council’s learning ecosystem; you will bring the learning technology expertise and technical judgment that help turn those choices into practical, sustainable solutions.
Our programs serve different audiences, funders and learning goals, and learning paths are not always linear. A learner may enter through an assessment or survey, browse a catalog, receive a recommendation, or move through content based on outcomes, competencies or prior activity. The platform is already built to support complexity that conventional learning management systems do not easily accommodate. You will build on that foundation as learner needs and program use cases evolve.
This role will appeal to someone who enjoys exploring technology and building useful products, and who is equally curious about the people, business needs and practical constraints behind them. blocks.text: About the National Council for Mental Wellbeing

The vision of the National Council for Mental Wellbeing is to make mental wellbeing, including recovery from substance use challenges, a reality for everyone. Despite overwhelming need, nearly 30 million people across the U.S. do not have access to comprehensive mental health and substance use treatment.

Founded in 1969, the National Council is a 501(c)(3) membership organization that drives policy and social change on behalf of more than 3,100 mental health and substance use treatment organizations and the more than 10 million children, adults and families they serve. We advocate for policies to ensure equitable access to high-quality services, build the capacity of mental health and substance use treatment organizations, and promote greater understanding of mental wellbeing as a core component of health and health care. Through Mental Health First Aid (MHFA), we have trained more than 4.5 million people in the U.S. to identify, understand and respond to signs and symptoms of mental health and substance use challenges.
The National Council operates as a remote-first organization, with employees working from locations across the United States.
The Opportunity

jobs.title: VP Product Innovation, Modern Campus
jobs.text:
About Modern Campus
Modern Campus empowers institutions to move with confidence across the modern learner journey. Our platform spans web content management, curriculum and catalog management, student engagement and lifelong learning — giving more than 1,700 colleges and universities the infrastructure they need to support the entire learner-to-earner lifecycle and deliver personalized, scalable experiences.
We partner with the education community to create new pathways for learning and opportunity, reimagining how institutions serve the modern learner and shape the future of education.
Our purpose — our north star — is to empower institutions to confidently serve and support the modern learner.
This mission and purpose come to life through how we show up every day:
We exist to create empowerment through education.
We lead with honesty and empathy.
We shape the future through innovation.
We become trusted partners.
We make the complex feel possible.
Position Summary
Modern Campus is seeking a visionary and execution-oriented Vice President, Product Innovation to identify, validate, build, and scale new product opportunities while transforming how we develop products through AI-enabled and agentic practices.
This leader will serve as the company's innovation catalyst, balancing customer discovery, strategic product incubation, and organizational transformation. The Vice President, Product Innovation will lead the creation of new offerings that expand our portfolio while establishing scalable, AI-native product development capabilities that accelerate speed, quality, and customer value across the organization.
The role partners closely with Product Management, Engineering, Design, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Executive Leadership to drive growth through both new products and new ways of building products.
What You'll Do
Product Innovation & New Venture Development
Identify, validate, and launch innovative software products that address emerging challenges and opportunities in higher education.
Lead customer discovery, market research, and rapid experimentation to assess new market opportunities.
Build and test MVPs, prototypes, and pilot programs to validate customer demand and commercial viability.
Define business models, pricing strategies, and go-to-market approaches for new offerings.
Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams to successfully transition validated concepts into scalable businesses.
Develop and manage an innovation portfolio that balances incremental improvements with transformative growth opportunities.
Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, and innovation across the product organization.
AI-Enabled Product Development Leadership
Define and champion Modern Campus's vision for AI-enabled and agentic product development.
Establish best practices for leveraging AI across the product lifecycle, including customer research, discovery, requirements gathering, prototyping, documentation, testing, experimentation, and product operations.
Evaluate emerging AI technologies and identify opportunities to improve how product teams operate and deliver value.
Develop repeatable frameworks, playbooks, governance models, and adoption strategies for responsible AI implementation.
Partner with Product, Engineering, and Design leaders to embed AI-native practices into day-to-day product development workflows.
Measure and continuously improve the impact of AI-enabled practices on customer outcomes, delivery speed, and organizational effectiveness.
Promote a culture of experimentation, continuous learning, and responsible AI adoption across the company.
Executive Leadership & Collaboration
Influence company strategy through innovation insights, customer feedback, and emerging market opportunities.
Communicate vision, strategy, business cases, and outcomes effectively to executive leadership and key stakeholders.
Build alignment across departments to accelerate innovation initiatives and organizational transformation.
Serve as a thought leader on AI, product innovation, and emerging technology trends.
What You'll Bring
Required Qualifications
Proven experience leading software products from concept through customer validation, commercial launch, and post-launch scaling.
Experience building and managing innovation portfolios, product incubators, or venture-style product development initiatives.
Demonstrated success delivering revenue-generating software products, including business model development, pricing strategy, and go-to-market execution.
Deep understanding of artificial intelligence technologies and their application to software product development.
Hands-on experience leveraging AI tools and agentic workflows to accelerate product development and decision-making.
Strong executive presence and communication skills with the ability to influence strategy and organizational change.
Proven ability to operate effectively in fast-paced, ambiguous, and rapidly evolving environments.
10+ years of progressive product leadership experience within a software organization.
Experience leading cross-functional teams, major product launches, and strategic initiatives.
Preferred Qualifications
MBA or advanced business degree.
Experience in higher education, education technology, SaaS, or other complex B2B software markets.
Experience scaling AI-enabled product organizations.
Track record of launching net-new businesses, platforms, or product categories.
Success in This Role
Within the first 12–24 months, successful outcomes may include:
Launching three or more new product experiments into market.
Creating a repeatable and measurable innovation pipeline from idea to commercialization.
Generating meaningful new revenue streams from newly launched offerings.
Increasing product team effectiveness through AI-enabled workflows and agentic development practices.
Improving speed-to-market and customer value realization across the product portfolio.
Establishing Modern Campus as a leader in AI-enabled product innovation within higher education technology.
Why Join Modern Campus?
At Modern Campus, we're transforming how higher education institutions engage learners throughout the entire student lifecycle. We believe innovation happens when talented people are empowered to experiment, challenge assumptions, and create solutions that make a meaningful impact.
This role offers a unique opportunity to shape both what we build and how we build it, driving the future of product innovation and AI-enabled development across the organization.
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
At Modern Campus, we believe that a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace strengthens relevance, resilience, and long-term success. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and identities to apply.
Modern Campus is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other protected status. If you require accommodation during any stage of the interview process, please let our recruiting team know.
* Our salary ranges reflect the minimum and maximum target for new hires for the position within the US and Canada. Within the range, individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
