jobs.title: Vice President, Software Engineering
jobs.text:
Career-defining. Life-changing.
At iRhythm, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your skills and your career while impacting the lives of people around the world. iRhythm is shaping a future where everyone, everywhere can access the best possible cardiac health solutions. Every day, we collaborate, create, and constantly reimagine what’s possible. We think big and move fast, driven by our commitment to put patients first and improve lives. We need builders like you. Curious and innovative problem solvers looking for the chance to meaningfully shape the future of cardiac health, our company, and your career
About This Role:
iRhythm is seeking a Vice President of Software Engineering to provide technical and organizational leadership across our regulated software platforms. Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Systems Development, this leader is accountable for ensuring the successful delivery, performance, and scalability of software products and platforms. These solutions enable clinician workflows, enhance patient experiences, integrate connected medical devices, and provide the data infrastructure necessary to support innovation, operational excellence, and growth. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution at scale, requiring executive leadership and offering exceptional visibility across the organization.
Key Responsibilities
Software Delivery & Operational Execution
Lead end-to-end software engineering execution across clinical, patient-facing, platform, and device-integrated software systems within a highly regulated Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) environment.
Establish and continuously evolve the engineering operating systems, governance frameworks, and development practices that enable disciplined planning, transparent execution, effective risk management, and predictable delivery across a complex software portfolio.
Champion continuous improvement initiatives that measurably enhance engineering velocity, product quality, release confidence, system reliability, and customer outcomes.
Ensure software development lifecycle processes consistently meet regulatory, compliance, and quality standards, including FDA, IEC 62304, ISO 13485, cybersecurity, and internal Quality Management System (QMS) requirements.
Translate complex technical concepts, delivery risks, and strategic tradeoffs into clear, actionable insights for executive leadership and key stakeholders.
Advance software engineering capabilities through scalable CI/CD frameworks, development platforms, automation, and engineering enablement tools appropriate for regulated medical technology environments.
Lead the responsible adoption and governance of AI-assisted software development practices to accelerate innovation, enhance productivity, improve quality, and reduce delivery risk.
Establish a metrics-driven engineering culture by leveraging meaningful operational and quality indicators to increase transparency, predictability, accountability, and data-informed decision making.
Team Development & Leadership
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing organization of software engineering directors, managers, and senior technical leaders, fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, and execution excellence.
Serve as a thought leader, trusted advisor and mentor to engineering leaders, cultivating leadership capability, organizational resilience, and a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and technical excellence across the company.
Cross-Functional & Strategic Contributions
Partner closely with executive and functional leaders across Product Security, Software Quality, Research & Systems Engineering, Machine Learning, and IT to ensure seamless execution, architectural alignment, and delivery excellence across the product portfolio.
Drive alignment and shared accountability across Product Management, Clinical, Quality, Regulatory, and other cross-functional teams to successfully deliver innovative solutions from concept through commercialization.
Lead software engineering diligence, technical assessments, and post-acquisition integration activities in support of the company's mergers and acquisitions strategy.
Contribute to the development and execution of the long-term software platform, architecture, and technology strategy, ensuring scalability, innovation, and competitive differentiation.
Qualifications
Required Experience
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive software engineering leadership experience, including leadership of large-scale engineering organizations and senior technology leaders.
Demonstrated success leading the development and delivery of Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) solutions within highly regulated medical device environments.
Proven track record bringing complex regulated software products from concept and development through verification, validation, regulatory approval, commercialization, and post-market support.
Deep expertise in FDA software regulations, IEC 62304, ISO 13485, and medical device quality systems, with a strong understanding of applying these requirements within modern software development environments.
Experience leading complex, matrixed software engineering organizations through periods of growth, transformation, organizational change, and technology modernization.
Preferred Experience
Experience spanning both high-growth and established healthcare, medical device, digital health, or regulated technology organizations.
Experience scaling software organizations supporting connected products, cloud platforms, data ecosystems, and customer-facing applications.
Exposure to technical diligence, integration planning, or software leadership support for mergers and acquisitions.
Demonstrated success modernizing software delivery capabilities, including CI/CD frameworks, automation, and engineering productivity tools within regulated environments.
Practical experience evaluating, implementing, and governing AI-assisted software development practices to improve engineering effectiveness, product quality, and delivery outcomes.
Leadership Profile
Strategic and execution-oriented leader with the ability to translate business priorities into operational excellence and measurable outcomes.
Equally comfortable shaping long-term technology strategy and engaging directly in delivery execution, organizational design, and engineering operations.
Proven builder of high-performing teams and leadership talent, with a strong track record of developing leaders and creating a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Exceptional cross-functional collaborator capable of influencing executive stakeholders and aligning diverse teams around shared objectives.
Data-driven, pragmatic, and decisive, with the ability to balance speed, quality, regulatory compliance, and business impact.
Resilient and adaptable leader who thrives in complex environments and successfully leads organizations through change, growth, and transformation.
Location:
Remote - US
Actual compensation may vary depending on job-related factors including knowledge, skills, experience, and work location.
Estimated Pay Range
$278,000.00 - $361,000.00
As a part of our core values, we ensure an inclusive workforce. We welcome and celebrate people of all backgrounds, experiences, skills, and perspectives. iRhythm Technologies, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We will consider for employment all qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with all applicable laws.
iRhythm provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in job application procedures, including those who may have any difficulty using our online system. If you need such an accommodation, you may contact us at
About iRhythm Technologies
iRhythm is a leading digital healthcare company that creates trusted solutions that detect, predict, and prevent disease. Combining wearable biosensors and cloud-based data analytics with powerful proprietary algorithms, iRhythm distills data from millions of heartbeats into clinically actionable information. Through a relentless focus on patient care, iRhythm’s vision is to deliver better data, better insights, and better health for all.
Make iRhythm your path forward. Zio, the heart monitor that changed the game.

jobs.title: Firm-wide Data Governance - Data Quality and Data Contracts - Vice President
jobs.text:
You will drive the execution of data governance across large-scale initiatives. This role sits at the center of improving data quality, strengthening controls, and enabling teams to manage data effectively. You will influence outcomes by ensuring data is governed with consistency and accountability.
As a Data Quality Governance Lead in the Firmwide Data Governance Function, you will lead the design and implementation of comprehensive data governance frameworks that ensure data integrity, quality, and compliance across the organization. Your role is pivotal in shaping the strategic direction of data management practices, influencing operational and business decisions that extend beyond immediate outcomes. You will leverage your deep expertise in regulatory compliance and data quality to mitigate risks and safeguard our reputation. By fostering collaboration across diverse teams, you will drive the adoption of best practices and innovative solutions, ensuring our data assets are responsibly managed and aligned with business goals. Your leadership will empower teams to navigate complex data challenges, enhancing our operational efficiency and supporting sustainable growth.
Job responsibilities
Develop and enforce data quality governance policies and standards to ensure compliance with data quality standards
Lead the design and implementation of data quality controls and data contracts for firm's most important data
Establish governance strategy, operating model, and ownership
Oversee adoption and implementation of data quality controls and data contracts for critical data elements along the lineage
Partner with CDOs, Data Owners, product, and technology teams to implement and enhance tooling solutions
Lead governance forums and cross-functional engagement to data quality and data contracts implementation across the bank for scoped activities.
Resolve complex data issues by identifying root causes and implementing effective solutions
Drive the adoption of change management initiatives, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation in data governance practices
Build knowledge of how business areas, architecture, applications, data platforms, and infrastructure integrate to accomplish business goals
Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
8 years of experience or equivalent expertise in designing and implementing data governance frameworks and policies
Experience in data, analytics, or product roles supporting data governance outcomes
Hands on experience in driving data quality transformation programs including data quality controls, data contracts, and lineage
Experience implementing enterprise Data Quality controls and monitoring frameworks
Experience with industry tools like Collibra, Snowflake, Databricks
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with cross-functional and multi-disciplinary teams
Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and project management skills

jobs.title: Director of Product Operations
jobs.text:
Join Revive Media to help advertisers across the country scale their localized Connected TV advertising. Our business is growing rapidly and we're in the midst of transforming from a services agency to a product-led business with our new native platform, Convoy. The platform is live with external partners and we're expanding its reach — this role will help us build the operational backbone that lets our product team scale as we grow.
We are a small, remote-first team of high-performing professionals with diverse backgrounds located across many time zones, including North America, Europe, and Asia. We prioritize asynchronous communication and documentation but come together as a team to solve hard problems.
The Role
You'll manage and develop our product team, partnering with lead product managers and executive leadership to translate product strategy into a sequenced roadmap and clear priorities for each squad. Lead product managers and leadership will identify strategic opportunities and set product direction; you'll translate that direction into team priorities, capacity decisions, and operating rhythms. Your squad-leading PMs will remain responsible for understanding their customers, validating solutions, and delivering measurable outcomes. You'll continuously improve how the product team plans, delivers, communicates, and handles support and escalations as the organization scales.
Responsibilities
People Leadership
Hire, coach, and develop the product management team against a clear leveling framework
Partner with product leadership and lead product managers to translate priorities into team capacity and ownership
Product Operations
Build and run the planning and delivery cadence that keeps the team's work aligned to company priorities and gives the rest of the organization reliable visibility into what's shipping and when
Establish consistent standards for specs, QA, definition of done, releases, and outcome tracking
Define and maintain a consistent approach to tracking expected and actual outcomes at the team and feature level, using those insights to improve future product decisions
Lead how production issues, escalations, and urgent requests are routed and resolved across product, engineering, and the teams that surface them
Continuously improve the systems the product team uses for planning, delivery, support, and communication, using better processes, tooling, and automation to reduce friction and coordination as the organization scales
Operate as a player-coach: step in hands-on where needed while building the team's judgment and capability
Cross-Functional Leadership
Partner with lead product managers to represent product in company-wide planning and communication
Build strong working relationships across engineering, design, GTM, customer success, and company leadership
What success looks like:
One year in, the product organization runs more predictably because of this person, and it shows up everywhere downstream: product managers, engineering, and the broader company all feel it.
Every squad and feature has a clear before-and-after: what outcome we expected, what actually happened, and product managers can point to their own impact using that data
Product managers on the team are growing, doing better work, and can see the difference their work makes
Production issues and escalations get resolved through a clear process instead of interrupting whoever happens to be closest, and product managers spend less time on it than they did a year ago
Releases require less last-minute coordination, and shared standards around specs, QA, and definition of done make delivery consistent across the team
The planning cadence gives the rest of the company reliable visibility into what's shipping and when, and other teams trust product's timelines more than they used to
As the team scales, its operating practices remain lightweight—providing greater clarity and consistency without slowing product managers down or pulling them away from customers and product work

jobs.title: Head of Product Management
jobs.text:
About Centric Software:
Centric Software® is a global leader, providing an innovative and AI-enabled product-concept-to-commercialization platform for retailers, brands and manufacturers of all sizes. We equip retail, fashion, luxury, footwear, outdoor, home and consumer goods brands with pioneering best-of-breed solutions to plan, design, develop, source, comply, buy, make, price, allocate, sell and replenish products. Our technology powers brands to streamline processes, drive efficiency and operate with confidence in an ever-changing market.
Our story is one of rapid growth, bold ideas and extraordinary opportunities. We’re here to challenge the status quo—and we’re looking for brilliant people who want to do the same. No matter where you are in the world, this is your chance to be part of something exceptional.
The Opportunity
Shoppingfeed, part of Centric Software, is looking for an experienced product leader to define and execute the next phase of our product strategy.
This is an exciting opportunity to lead the Product Management function for one of the leading product feed management and marketplace syndication platforms. You will own the product vision, roadmap and strategy while leading a team of Product Managers responsible for delivering innovative solutions that help retailers and brands distribute product data across marketplaces, comparison engines and social commerce channels.
Reporting to the VP of Product (PXM), you will act as the product leader for Shoppingfeed, ensuring its strategy aligns with the wider Product Experience Management (PXM) vision while continuing to innovate as a market-leading platform.
About the Team
The Shoppingfeed Product team is based primarily in France and works closely with Engineering, Customer Success, Sales and the wider PXM organisation.
You’ll lead a team of four Product Managers while collaborating closely with the Head of Engineering to deliver a unified vision across Product and Technology.
What You Will Be Doing
Own the product vision, strategy and roadmap for Shoppingfeed.
Lead and mentor a team of Product Managers, providing coaching, career development and organisational leadership.
Ensure product investments align with both customer needs and Centric Software’s wider PXM strategy.
Translate customer feedback, market trends and competitive insights into an executable roadmap.
Act as the product spokesperson internally and externally, communicating product direction with clarity and confidence.
Partner closely with Engineering to ensure successful delivery of strategic initiatives.
Build strong relationships across Product, Sales, Customer Success and Marketing.
Create stronger alignment between Shoppingfeed and the broader PXM portfolio.
Drive prioritisation decisions based on business value, customer impact and technical feasibility.
Foster a collaborative, customer-first product culture focused on innovation and execution.
What We’re Looking For
Proven experience leading Product Management teams within enterprise SaaS.
Experience managing Product Managers and developing high-performing teams.
Strong strategic thinking combined with excellent execution skills.
Experience defining product roadmaps and long-term product vision.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills.
Ability to influence across technical and commercial teams.
Experience presenting product strategy to senior leadership.
Nice to Have
Experience in Product Feed Management, Marketplace Syndication, eCommerce or Product Information Management (PIM).
Knowledge of Product Experience Management (PXM).
Understanding of digital commerce, retail technology or marketplace ecosystems.
Fluent French speaking.
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Technology or a related discipline.
10+ years’ experience in Product Management.
Several years leading Product teams within enterprise software.
Centric Software provides equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, color, age, religion, protected veteran or disability status or genetic information.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.text:
Driftrock is hiring a Head of Product to set the direction for our platform and lead the team building the products that help automotive brands and dealers deliver the world's best experience for finding, buying and owning a car.
Quick facts
Team: Product, leading our Product team and working daily with Engineering, Design, Customer Success and Commercial
Product: The whole Driftrock platform across Capture, Convert and Connect, plus our internal tooling
Reports to: CEO
Direct reports: Our Product Manager(s), with room to grow the team
Location: Fully remote, UK or abroad, with a few hours of daily UK overlap
Contract: Full time, permanent
Salary: £85,000 to £105,000, plus share options
Start date: As soon as you're ready
Why this role exists
Driftrock powers customer acquisition for some of the world's biggest automotive brands and dealers, including BMW, BYD, Mercedes-Benz and Volvo. Since 2013 we've built a platform that captures enquiries from every channel a car buyer touches, validates them in real time, nurtures them through messaging journeys, and measures everything through to the vehicle sale.
That work enables billions of euros in vehicle sales every year and makes buying a car a better experience for consumers.
The next 12 months are set to be the biggest in our history. We're preparing to launch our boldest products yet, growing across Europe, bringing our platform to more customers, and putting AI at the heart of how our products work.
This calls for a product leader who can set a clear direction, make the big calls on where we focus, and build a product team that turns strategy into shipped, measured outcomes. As our Product team scales, this role will take increasing ownership of product direction and decision-making from the CEO. Reporting to the CEO, you'll shape the future of the platform and help define how car buyers and car sellers connect.
What you'll own
You'll be accountable for Driftrock's product strategy and the results it delivers. That means deciding why and what we build across the whole platform and our internal tooling, leading and growing the product team that delivers it, and making sure every major bet ships and moves the metrics that matter to our customers and our business. You'll work closely with the CEO as ownership of day-to-day product leadership transitions into the Product team.
*Your first 90 days*
By day 30: you've met customers, partners and every team, used the platform end to end, got to know the Product team, and mapped the current landscape: our products, how brands and dealers use them, how product work flows today, and where the biggest opportunities sit.
By day 60: you've agreed a product strategy and 12-month roadmap with the CEO and leadership team, set up a clear product operating rhythm with Engineering and Design, and agreed goals and development plans with each person in your team.
By day 90: discovery to delivery runs on a predictable cadence, the whole company can see what's coming and why, your first measurable product win has shipped, and you have a plan for how the product team grows next. You and the CEO are aligned on the direction for the next stage of Driftrock's product growth.
What you'll be doing
Set the product vision and strategy for the Driftrock platform, turning company goals into a clear, evidence-backed roadmap the whole company understands.
Lead, coach and grow the Product team, setting high standards for discovery, decision-making and delivery, and hiring well as the team expands. We're open to strong Senior or Lead Product Managers who are ready to step up into broader product leadership.
Make the big prioritisation calls across customer-facing products and internal tooling, balancing customer value, commercial impact and technical health so Engineering always works on what matters most.
Take new products from first discovery to market, each with a clear launch plan and success measures.
Solution design alongside Product Managers and other stakeholders. We are a small team, so this Head of Product role is a chance to be hands-on whilst leading and growing the team.
Stay close to customers, spending time with brands, dealers and partners every month so real evidence shapes every major decision.
Build a product operating model that scales, with shared rituals, metrics and tools that help a remote team move quickly and stay aligned.
Partner with Commercial, Marketing and Customer Success on pricing, packaging, positioning and launches, so what we build lands well and grows revenue.
Report on product performance to the CEO and board, showing clearly what we shipped, what it changed and what we learned.
What you'll bring
A track record of leading product for a B2B SaaS platform, ideally combined with experience in consumer product or product-led growth, with a strategy that measurably grew revenue, retention or a core customer metric.
Experience managing and developing product managers, and building a team where people do their best work. Strong Senior or Lead Product Managers ready to take this next step are encouraged to apply.
Evidence of taking a new product or major bet from first discovery through to a successful launch.
Strong product judgement: you make clear, well-reasoned calls on what not to build as well as what to build, and bring people with you.
A habit of regular customer discovery, and comfort combining customer insight with product and commercial data to make decisions. You have a strong experimental and data-driven mindset.
The ability to work closely with engineering and design leaders on technical trade-offs, sequencing and delivery.
Clear written and spoken communication, from a one-page strategy to a board update, in a remote, async-friendly team.
Comfort being hands-on when it helps, from writing a brief to digging into the data yourself. You take a collaborative, pragmatic approach to leadership and are comfortable getting into the details when needed.
Experience working in a smaller, fast-growing company rather than exclusively in a large, highly structured enterprise environment.
Bonus points
Experience with marketing technology, lead generation, messaging or CRM-adjacent products.
Knowledge of the automotive or e-mobility industry, especially how brands and dealers work together.
Experience shipping AI-powered products, or using AI tools heavily across discovery and delivery.
Experience launching products into new markets.
Experience shaping pricing and packaging for a SaaS product
Not sure you tick every box? Please apply anyway. We value different perspectives, backgrounds and career paths, and we're interested in what you could bring to the role, not just whether you've followed a traditional route into product leadership.
Why Driftrock
Driftrock's mission is to become the world-leading automotive and e-mobility marketing software platform, and help accelerate the transition to clean transport.
We work with some of the world's biggest brands, including BMW, BYD, Mercedes-Benz and Volvo, and partner with the world's leading platforms, including Meta, Google, mobile.de and Auto Trader.
We've been building since 2013, and our work enables billions of euros in vehicle sales every year.
We're a close, fully remote team of 45 people across engineering, design, customer success, performance and commercial, spread across the world.
That means your work has a real, visible impact on our product, our culture and how we operate.
We're at the cutting edge of marketing technology, with plenty of room to unlock value from data and to help speed up the shift to electric vehicles.
How we work is shaped by four values:
We care: about our team, our customers, and the people who see the marketing messages that we power. Work isn't done until we can prove it's useful to both the consumer and the customer.
Be that person: if something needs fixing, fix it. It's never someone else's problem.
People-first: we put people at the core of everything, and never compromise security or privacy for results.
Be better today than you were yesterday: we bake learning and continuous improvement into everything we do, for ourselves and our customers.
In practice, this looks like weekly Monday Showcases where we share what we're learning, regular retros, a budget to attend the courses and conferences that grow you, Donut coffee pairings to stay connected, and an annual company Summit that brings the whole global team together in person.
What's in it for you
We're remote-first and flexible about how and where you work, with co-working space available if you want it. Alongside your salary:
Share options in Driftrock, on founder-friendly, tax-efficient EMI terms, including the option to retain vested options after leaving (at board discretion).
Comprehensive Vitality health cover: medical, dental, vision, hearing, mental-health support and therapy, cancer cover, a free Headspace subscription and Vitality rewards.
24 to 28 days' holiday (24 + 1 extra each year, capped at 28), plus bank holidays.
Pension contributions, life assurance (3x salary) and income protection.
Electric car salary-sacrifice scheme (Octopus): save up to ~40%, with insurance, servicing and a charging perk included.
Enhanced maternity and paternity leave.
A learning budget for books, courses and conferences, plus time for personal goals.
Perks and discounts via CharlieHR, and a BMW Group employee discount programme.
Outside the UK?
We're remote-first and hire globally. While some UK-specific benefits are delivered differently abroad, we strive for genuine parity. Wherever you are, the standard package includes a comprehensive health plan, pension contributions, paid time off including local bank holidays, share options, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, a learning budget, and our flexible working culture. International team members are employed compliantly via an Employer of Record (Remote.com).
Our hiring process
A short intro call with our team.
A conversation with our CEO about the role and how you lead the product.
A live, interactive workshop or pairing session based on a real Driftrock product challenge, rather than a take-home task.
A final conversation with the team, including Engineering and Product.
Inclusion at Driftrock
Driftrock is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background, identity and life experience, and we're building a team that reflects the people our marketing reaches. We don't make decisions based on age, disability, gender, gender identity, marital status, race or ethnicity, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. If you need any adjustments to the application or interview process to do your best, just let us know, and we're glad to help.
We will not be considering recruitment agencies for this role.
By applying for this job you give us permission to store your data on our secure applicant tracking system and to contact you about Driftrock job opportunities. We process your data for recruitment purposes only and keep it until this role is filled, after which we will delete it or, with your agreement, keep it for similar future roles for up to 12 months. See our privacy policy at driftrock.com/privacy-policy for how we comply with GDPR, including how to access, correct, delete or restrict the data we hold. You can lodge a complaint with the UK supervisory authority (the Information Commissioner's Office), or contact our DPO for any concerns.

Direct reports: Our Product Manager(s), with room to grow the team
Location: Fully remote, UK or abroad, with a few hours of daily UK overlap
Contract: Full time, permanent
Salary: £85,000 to £105,000, plus share options
Start date: As soon as you're ready

blocks.text: Why this role exists

Driftrock powers customer acquisition for some of the world's biggest automotive brands and dealers, including BMW, BYD, Mercedes-Benz and Volvo. Since 2013 we've built a platform that captures enquiries from every channel a car buyer touches, validates them in real time, nurtures them through messaging journeys, and measures everything through to the vehicle sale.
That work enables billions of euros in vehicle sales every year and makes buying a car a better experience for consumers.

The next 12 months are set to be the biggest in our history. We're preparing to launch our boldest products yet, growing across Europe, bringing our platform to more customers, and putting AI at the heart of how our products work.

This calls for a product leader who can set a clear direction, make the big calls on where we focus, and build a product team that turns strategy into shipped, measured outcomes. As our Product team scales, this role will take increasing ownership of product direction and decision-making from the CEO. Reporting to the CEO, you'll shape the future of the platform and help define how car buyers and car sellers connect.
What you'll own

You'll be accountable for Driftrock's product strategy and the results it delivers. That means deciding why and what we build across the whole platform and our internal tooling, leading and growing the product team that delivers it, and making sure every major bet ships and moves the metrics that matter to our customers and our business. You'll work closely with the CEO as ownership of day-to-day product leadership transitions into the Product team.
*Your first 90 days*

items: By day 30: you've met customers, partners and every team, used the platform end to end, got to know the Product team, and mapped the current landscape: our products, how brands and dealers use them, how product work flows today, and where the biggest opportunities sit.

By day 60: you've agreed a product strategy and 12-month roadmap with the CEO and leadership team, set up a clear product operating rhythm with Engineering and Design, and agreed goals and development plans with each person in your team.

By day 90: discovery to delivery runs on a predictable cadence, the whole company can see what's coming and why, your first measurable product win has shipped, and you have a plan for how the product team grows next. You and the CEO are aligned on the direction for the next stage of Driftrock's product growth.

blocks.text: What you'll be doing

items: Set the product vision and strategy for the Driftrock platform, turning company goals into a clear, evidence-backed roadmap the whole company understands.

Lead, coach and grow the Product team, setting high standards for discovery, decision-making and delivery, and hiring well as the team expands. We're open to strong Senior or Lead Product Managers who are ready to step up into broader product leadership.

Make the big prioritisation calls across customer-facing products and internal tooling, balancing customer value, commercial impact and technical health so Engineering always works on what matters most.
Take new products from first discovery to market, each with a clear launch plan and success measures.
Solution design alongside Product Managers and other stakeholders. We are a small team, so this Head of Product role is a chance to be hands-on whilst leading and growing the team.
Stay close to customers, spending time with brands, dealers and partners every month so real evidence shapes every major decision.
Build a product operating model that scales, with shared rituals, metrics and tools that help a remote team move quickly and stay aligned.
Partner with Commercial, Marketing and Customer Success on pricing, packaging, positioning and launches, so what we build lands well and grows revenue.
Report on product performance to the CEO and board, showing clearly what we shipped, what it changed and what we learned.

blocks.text: What you'll bring

items: A track record of leading product for a B2B SaaS platform, ideally combined with experience in consumer product or product-led growth, with a strategy that measurably grew revenue, retention or a core customer metric.
Experience managing and developing product managers, and building a team where people do their best work. Strong Senior or Lead Product Managers ready to take this next step are encouraged to apply.
Evidence of taking a new product or major bet from first discovery through to a successful launch.
Strong product judgement: you make clear, well-reasoned calls on what not to build as well as what to build, and bring people with you.
A habit of regular customer discovery, and comfort combining customer insight with product and commercial data to make decisions. You have a strong experimental and data-driven mindset.
The ability to work closely with engineering and design leaders on technical trade-offs, sequencing and delivery.
Clear written and spoken communication, from a one-page strategy to a board update, in a remote, async-friendly team.

Comfort being hands-on when it helps, from writing a brief to digging into the data yourself. You take a collaborative, pragmatic approach to leadership and are comfortable getting into the details when needed.
Experience working in a smaller, fast-growing company rather than exclusively in a large, highly structured enterprise environment.

blocks.text: Bonus points

items: Experience with marketing technology, lead generation, messaging or CRM-adjacent products.
Knowledge of the automotive or e-mobility industry, especially how brands and dealers work together.
Experience shipping AI-powered products, or using AI tools heavily across discovery and delivery.
Experience launching products into new markets.
Experience shaping pricing and packaging for a SaaS product

blocks.text: Not sure you tick every box? Please apply anyway. We value different perspectives, backgrounds and career paths, and we're interested in what you could bring to the role, not just whether you've followed a traditional route into product leadership.
Why Driftrock
Driftrock's mission is to become the world-leading automotive and e-mobility marketing software platform, and help accelerate the transition to clean transport.
We work with some of the world's biggest brands, including BMW, BYD, Mercedes-Benz and Volvo, and partner with the world's leading platforms, including Meta, Google, mobile.de and Auto Trader.
We've been building since 2013, and our work enables billions of euros in vehicle sales every year.
We're a close, fully remote team of 45 people across engineering, design, customer success, performance and commercial, spread across the world.
That means your work has a real, visible impact on our product, our culture and how we operate.
We're at the cutting edge of marketing technology, with plenty of room to unlock value from data and to help speed up the shift to electric vehicles.
How we work is shaped by four values:

items: We care: about our team, our customers, and the people who see the marketing messages that we power. Work isn't done until we can prove it's useful to both the consumer and the customer.
Be that person: if something needs fixing, fix it. It's never someone else's problem.
People-first: we put people at the core of everything, and never compromise security or privacy for results.
Be better today than you were yesterday: we bake learning and continuous improvement into everything we do, for ourselves and our customers.

blocks.text: In practice, this looks like weekly Monday Showcases where we share what we're learning, regular retros, a budget to attend the courses and conferences that grow you, Donut coffee pairings to stay connected, and an annual company Summit that brings the whole global team together in person.
What's in it for you
We're remote-first and flexible about how and where you work, with co-working space available if you want it. Alongside your salary:

items: Share options in Driftrock, on founder-friendly, tax-efficient EMI terms, including the option to retain vested options after leaving (at board discretion).
Comprehensive Vitality health cover: medical, dental, vision, hearing, mental-health support and therapy, cancer cover, a free Headspace subscription and Vitality rewards.
24 to 28 days' holiday (24 + 1 extra each year, capped at 28), plus bank holidays.
Pension contributions, life assurance (3x salary) and income protection.
Electric car salary-sacrifice scheme (Octopus): save up to ~40%, with insurance, servicing and a charging perk included.
Enhanced maternity and paternity leave.
A learning budget for books, courses and conferences, plus time for personal goals.
Perks and discounts via CharlieHR, and a BMW Group employee discount programme.

blocks.text: Outside the UK?

We're remote-first and hire globally. While some UK-specific benefits are delivered differently abroad, we strive for genuine parity. Wherever you are, the standard package includes a comprehensive health plan, pension contributions, paid time off including local bank holidays, share options, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, a learning budget, and our flexible working culture. International team members are employed compliantly via an Employer of Record (Remote.com).
Our hiring process

items: A short intro call with our team.
A conversation with our CEO about the role and how you lead the product.
A live, interactive workshop or pairing session based on a real Driftrock product challenge, rather than a take-home task.
A final conversation with the team, including Engineering and Product.

blocks.text: Inclusion at Driftrock

Driftrock is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background, identity and life experience, and we're building a team that reflects the people our marketing reaches. We don't make decisions based on age, disability, gender, gender identity, marital status, race or ethnicity, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. If you need any adjustments to the application or interview process to do your best, just let us know, and we're glad to help.
We will not be considering recruitment agencies for this role.

By applying for this job you give us permission to store your data on our secure applicant tracking system and to contact you about Driftrock job opportunities. We process your data for recruitment purposes only and keep it until this role is filled, after which we will delete it or, with your agreement, keep it for similar future roles for up to 12 months. See our privacy policy at driftrock.com/privacy-policy for how we comply with GDPR, including how to access, correct, delete or restrict the data we hold. You can lodge a complaint with the UK supervisory authority (the Information Commissioner's Office), or contact our DPO for any concerns.

jobs.title: Firm-wide Data Governance - Data Quality and Data Contracts - Vice President
jobs.text:
You will drive the execution of data governance across large-scale initiatives. This role sits at the center of improving data quality, strengthening controls, and enabling teams to manage data effectively. You will influence outcomes by ensuring data is governed with consistency and accountability.
As a Data Quality Governance Lead in the Firmwide Data Governance Function, you will lead the design and implementation of comprehensive data governance frameworks that ensure data integrity, quality, and compliance across the organization. Your role is pivotal in shaping the strategic direction of data management practices, influencing operational and business decisions that extend beyond immediate outcomes. You will leverage your deep expertise in regulatory compliance and data quality to mitigate risks and safeguard our reputation. By fostering collaboration across diverse teams, you will drive the adoption of best practices and innovative solutions, ensuring our data assets are responsibly managed and aligned with business goals. Your leadership will empower teams to navigate complex data challenges, enhancing our operational efficiency and supporting sustainable growth.
Job responsibilities
Develop and enforce data quality governance policies and standards to ensure compliance with data quality standards
Lead the design and implementation of data quality controls and data contracts for firm's most important data
Establish governance strategy, operating model, and ownership
Oversee adoption and implementation of data quality controls and data contracts for critical data elements along the lineage
Partner with CDOs, Data Owners, product, and technology teams to implement and enhance tooling solutions
Lead governance forums and cross-functional engagement to data quality and data contracts implementation across the bank for scoped activities.
Resolve complex data issues by identifying root causes and implementing effective solutions
Drive the adoption of change management initiatives, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation in data governance practices
Build knowledge of how business areas, architecture, applications, data platforms, and infrastructure integrate to accomplish business goals
Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
8 years of experience or equivalent expertise in designing and implementing data governance frameworks and policies
Experience in data, analytics, or product roles supporting data governance outcomes
Hands on experience in driving data quality transformation programs including data quality controls, data contracts, and lineage
Experience implementing enterprise Data Quality controls and monitoring frameworks
Experience with industry tools like Collibra, Snowflake, Databricks
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with cross-functional and multi-disciplinary teams
Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and project management skills

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.text:
BrightHire is a category-creating, high-growth, Series B software company with a mission to give everyone the hiring experience they deserve.
We deliver on this mission by transforming the way many of the world’s leading companies build exceptional teams. We created the Interview Intelligence category, and our clients include some of the world’s most innovative companies—Canva, OpenAI, Ramp, Hubspot—up to the Fortune 500.
BrightHire is building a leading AI-native hiring platform.
We created the Interview Intelligence category by applying conversation intelligence to how companies evaluate and hire talent. Today, hundreds of organizations—from Ramp and Canva to SAP and HCA Healthcare —use BrightHire to make better hiring decisions, improve interviewer performance, and deliver stronger candidate experiences.
BrightHire is now part of Zoom and operates as a stand-alone business unit. This gives us a rare combination of startup velocity and global scale. We are growing more than 100% year over year, with significant opportunities to accelerate through Zoom’s technology, distribution, customer relationships, and broader platform.
We currently have two rapidly growing products:
BrightHire Interview: Conversation intelligence for human-led interviews.
BrightHire Screen: An AI interviewer for structured candidate screening at scale.
This is only the beginning. Our ambition is to become one of the three most consequential hiring platforms in the world.
The Opportunity
We are looking for an exceptional Head of Product to lead BrightHire’s next chapter.
You will be our senior-most product leader, responsible for helping determine where we play, how we win, and how we translate our ambition into products that create meaningful customer and business impact.
You will rapidly build context across our customers, products, technology, market, competitive landscape, and commercial model. From that context, you will develop a clear point of view about the opportunities that matter most and translate it into a focused set of high-conviction product investments.
You will lead product across BrightHire Interview, BrightHire Screen, and future products. This will require difficult decisions about how to balance products with strong existing momentum, platform investments, and entirely new opportunities created by advances in AI.
A critical part of the role is bringing leverage to the CEO, Head of Engineering, and broader leadership team. You will bring clear recommendations, articulate the underlying reasoning and trade-offs, and help the organization make better and faster decisions about where to focus its resources.
You will also ensure that strategy translates into excellent execution. You will stay close to customers, active product work, roadmap decisions, product reviews, launches, and adoption—helping teams resolve ambiguity, raise product quality, and deliver meaningful outcomes.
You will work across Zoom to identify R&D, platform, go-to-market, and distribution synergies that can create differentiation and growth at a scale BrightHire could not achieve independently.
The goal is not to build a large product organization for its own sake. It is to build an exceptional product and business. The right candidate is motivated by customer impact, product quality, strategic advantage, and growth—not team size or span of control.
What You’ll Do
Define how BrightHire wins
Rapidly develop a deep understanding of our customers, products, market, technology, economics, and competitive position.
Develop a clear perspective on strategy – where BrightHire should play and how we can win.
Translate our strategy into a focused sequence of product investments.
Bring the CEO and leadership team clear points of view, recommendations, and trade-offs.
Continually reassess our assumptions and priorities as the market and technology evolves.
Lead a multi-product portfolio
Partner with the CEO and Head of Engineering on strategy, roadmap, resourcing, execution, launches, adoption, and business impact.
Allocate resources across BrightHire’s current products, platform capabilities, and new bets.
Ensure our largest initiatives have a clear customer, value proposition, competitive position, success measures, and path to meaningful impact.
Create the product and platform foundations required to expand BrightHire into a broader AI-native hiring platform.
Turn strategy into exceptional products
Translate strategic priorities into clear roadmaps, ownership, resource allocation, and execution.
Create a lightweight operating model that drives speed and quality.
Hold a high bar for product value, usability, reliability, and trust.
Stay close to workstreams to identify risks, resolve ambiguity, and maintain momentum.
Ensure products move successfully from insight and concept through launch, adoption, measurement, and iteration.
Build AI-native products
Identify opportunities that become possible as model capabilities improve.
Apply your experience building great AI products – prototyping, evaluations, reliability, trust, product economics, and continuous improvement.
Balance rapid innovation with the transparency, quality, and trust required for enterprise adoption.
Personally use and experiment with modern AI tools and workflows.
Turn product into growth
Connect roadmap decisions to adoption, retention, and revenue.
Partner with sales, marketing, and CS to translate product investments into revenue.
Participate in customer and prospect conversations and use them to sharpen product strategy.
Shape positioning, launches, enablement, adoption, and competitive narratives.
Identify opportunities to use Zoom’s tech, relationships, and distribution to accelerate growth.
Raise the bar across product
Be an insightful, high-leverage resource to product managers and designers, helping them sharpen their thinking, make better decisions, and produce stronger work.
Raise the quality of product strategy, judgment, craft, and execution across the team.
Build a culture of intellectual honesty, customer obsession, speed, and accountability.
What We’re Looking For
Strategic judgment
You quickly understand complex customers, markets, products, and technologies.
You identify what matters most and turn incomplete information into clear recommendations and trade-offs.
You can focus an organization around a few high-conviction product bets.
Commercial instincts
You connect product decisions to adoption, retention, revenue, and competitive advantage.
You are strong with customers and prospects and can distinguish broad market demand from isolated requests.
You understand how to build scalable enterprise products.
Product leadership
You have led significant products from strategy through launch, adoption, and measurable impact.
You have made difficult prioritization and resource-allocation decisions across multiple products or workstreams.
You raise the judgment, product craft, and effectiveness of PMs and designers.
AI product experience
You have successfully shipped AI-first products.
You understand model capabilities, evaluations, reliability, trust, economics, and customer value.
You actively use modern AI tools and stay close to advances in the field.
Execution excellence
You translate strategy into focused, high-quality execution without unnecessary process.
You stay close to the details that matter, resolve ambiguity, and maintain momentum.
You are decisive, dependable, and consistently raise the quality of the work.
Experience in recruiting technology or an adjacent hiring category is strongly preferred, but not required.
How You Operate
Hands-on: You want to build, not simply supervise. You stay close to customers, product experiences, and the work of the team while focusing your own time on the decisions and interventions that create the most leverage.
Positive and energizing: You bring urgency, optimism, and an attitude that raises the performance of the people around you.
Highly collaborative: You bring clear opinions without ego, engage constructively in disagreement, and earn trust through judgment and follow-through.
Passionate about hiring: You believe hiring is an important and underserved problem and are motivated to improve it for companies and candidates.
Competitive: You study the market, care deeply about pace, and want to build the product that defines the category—not merely participates in it.
*Note to Recruiters and Placement Agencies: We do not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward unsolicited agency resumes to our website. We will not pay fees to any third party agency or firm and will not be responsible for any agency fees associated with unsolicited resumes. Unsolicited resumes received will be considered our property.

jobs.title: Director, Product Planning
jobs.text:
At Ripple, we’re building a world where value moves like information does today. It’s big, it’s bold, and we’re already doing it. Through our crypto solutions for financial institutions, businesses, governments and developers, we are improving the global financial system and creating greater economic fairness and opportunity for more people, in more places around the world. And we get to do the best work of our career and grow our skills surrounded by colleagues who have our backs.
If you’re ready to see your impact and unlock incredible career growth opportunities, join us, and build real world value.
THE WORK:
The Director of Product Planning will act as the connection within our product group, converting strategy into a practical, well-ordered plan. This person keeps the product team coordinated, informed, and progressing effectively. This role offers high visibility and influence for someone wanting to engage with the full product organization.
You will not directly own a feature roadmap. Your role is to guide the process that aligns and prioritizes all product leaders’ roadmaps. The metrics themselves are created by our Data Science team. Your responsibility is to manage how these metrics are analyzed, communicated, and formed into a decisive narrative.
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Roadmap and Prioritization
Own the end-to-end planning process that turns strategic priorities into a resourced, sequenced roadmap across product lines
Facilitate tradeoff and prioritization discussions among product leaders, surfacing conflicts and dependencies before they become blockers
Keep the roadmap current and credible as priorities shift, and make sure changes are communicated clearly to collaborators
Cross-Functional Execution and Operating Rhythm
Build and manage the product org's operating rhythm — planning cycles, launch readiness reviews, cross-team syncs, retros
Own the tooling and systems (e.g., Jira, Linear, Notion) that keep planning artifacts organized and trustworthy as a single source of truth
Identify and resolve cross-team dependencies and process gaps before they slow down execution
Metrics Reporting and Synthesis
Partner closely with Data Science, who build and maintain the underlying metrics and dashboards
Own the reporting layer on top of the data. Pull the right numbers together, synthesize their meaning, and package them into clear, recurring updates for product and company leadership.
Translate data into recommendations and talking points — not just charts — to inform planning and prioritization decisions
Special Projects and Organizational Support
Serve as a versatile resource for the Senior Director of Product Management, leading cross-organizational initiatives, coordinating process enhancements, or conducting ad hoc analyses
Represent the product org's planning function in conversations with adjacent teams (engineering, build, legal/compliance, finance) as needed
WHAT YOU'LL BRING:
5+ years in product operations, technical program management, chief-of-staff, or a similar cross-functional planning role
Strong track record running planning/prioritization processes across multiple teams or product lines
Comfortable working with data and metrics, even if you do not build the underlying pipelines. You know how to ask Data Science the right questions. Then, you turn their output into a story.
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to synthesize complexity into something leadership can act on quickly
Highly organized, low-ego, and energized by making other people's work easier and more coherent
Experience leading or managing a team is a plus, though this role may start as an individual contributor
Experience in a fast paced, regulated, or high-stakes industry is a plus
For positions that will be based in CA, the annual salary range for this position is below. Actual salaries may vary based on numerous factors including, among other things, an individual applicant’s experience and qualifications for the position. This range does not include equity or additional compensation, such as bonuses or commissions.
CA Annual Base Salary Range
$248,000—$310,000 USD
WHO WE ARE:
Do Your Best Work
The opportunity to build in a fast-paced start-up environment with experienced industry leaders
A learning environment where you can dive deep into the latest technologies and make an impact. A professional development budget to support other modes of learning.
Thrive in an environment where no matter what race, ethnicity, gender, origin, or culture they identify with, every employee is a respected, valued, and empowered part of the team.
In-office collaboration for moments that matter is important to our culture, and we give managers and teams the flexibility to decide which 10+ days a month they come in.
Bi-weekly all-company meeting - business updates and ask me anything style discussion with our Leadership Team
We come together for moments that matter which include team offsites, team bonding activities, happy hours and more!
Take Control of Your Finances
Competitive salary, bonuses, and equity
Competitive benefits that cover physical and mental healthcare, retirement, family forming, and family support
Employee giving match
Mobile phone stipend
Take Care of Yourself
R&R days so you can rest and recharge
Generous wellness reimbursement and weekly onsite & virtual programming
Generous vacation policy - work with your manager to take time off when you need it
Industry-leading parental leave policies. Family planning benefits.
Catered lunches, fully-stocked kitchens with premium snacks/beverages, and plenty of fun events
Benefits listed above are for full-time employees.
Ripple is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We do not discriminate against qualified employees or applicants because of race, color, religion, gender identity, sex, sexual identity, pregnancy, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, marital status, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, military status, or any other characteristic protected by local law or ordinance.

jobs.title: Director, Scientific Data
jobs.text:
About the Role
Drug Hunter is a B2B scientific intelligence platform for biotech/pharma R&D scientists that empowers them to discover the medicines of the future. We serve >250 R&D institutions, including most of the top global biotech & pharma companies. We're a mission-driven, product-focused company backed by top-tier investors and trusted by the world's leading R&D organizations.
The Director, Scientific Data will own the integrity, structure, and evolution of Drug Hunter’s scientific data across our knowledge platform and scientific databases. You will lead the scientific data team within our Technical organization and be the bridge between our scientists and our engineers.
Key Responsibilities
Serve as the primary internal subject-matter expert for cheminformatics and scientific data, with sufficient breadth across bioinformatics and drug discovery data to guide data decisions spanning chemistry and biology.
Own the scientific strategy for how Drug Hunter acquires, represents, integrates, normalizes, and maintains scientific data, partnering with Engineering on the architecture and systems that operationalize that strategy and Science on both automated and manual data curation processes.
Define how chemical entities are represented, registered, standardized, and resolved across sources, and establish curation standards, controlled vocabularies, QA rules, and tooling that allows data curation to take place at scale
Define approaches for extracting structured scientific information from unstructured content, including chemical structures, text, and tables from literature and patents, and establish how extracted information should be linked to canonical entities.
Own the scientific semantics, entity resolution, and ontology strategy that unifies compound synonyms, target and gene nomenclature, disease terms, organizations, assays, and other scientific concepts across sources, including approaches for handling ambiguity and conflicting source assertions.
Evaluate scientific data sources across chemistry, biology, DMPK, drug, and clinical domains, assessing their coverage, scientific quality, overlap, limitations, licensing considerations, and update characteristics, and determine how they should contribute to Drug Hunter's data.
Establish standards for scientific data quality, provenance, validation, completeness, and freshness, and ensure the Data team has effective processes for identifying and resolving data-quality issues.
Partner closely with Science to translate scientific expertise and curation decisions into consistent, maintainable data models, standards, and processes.
Partner with Engineering to define data models and technical approaches that accurately represent complex scientific information and support the Drug Hunter platform, jointly evaluating architectural decisions and trade-offs where data and application systems intersect.
Partner with Product Management to translate scientific and technical requirements into project specifications for the data team and communicate the trade-offs the technical decisions carry.
Evaluate build-versus-buy decisions for scientific datasets, chem- and bio-informatics capabilities, and data tooling, partnering with Engineering where decisions involve shared technical infrastructure or application architecture.
Lead the Data team in translating scientific data priorities into executable projects, remaining sufficiently involved in day-to-day work to understand progress, technical challenges, dependencies, and workload.
Provide scientific and technical leadership, mentorship, and direction to the Data team, creating, hiring, and managing roles as needed.
Requirements
PhD in cheminformatics, bioinformatics, computational biology, structural biology, or a related quantitative life-science field.
10+ years working with scientific data in drug discovery, biotech, or life science data/informatics companies, including 3+ years leading people or a data function
Working cheminformatics literacy (molecular representations, structure standardization, substructure/similarity search concepts, RDKit or similar tools)
Fluency in bioinformatics, with a deep working knowledge of biological databases and ontologies, target and pathway biology, and gene/protein identifier mapping
Strong data modeling skills and hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL; experience with data pipelines and modern data tooling
Understanding of the drug discovery process from target to clinic, and ability to converse fluently with medicinal chemsits and biologists
Clear communicator who can move seamlessly between scientific details and engineering/product trade-offs
Benefits
Drug Hunter provides industry-leading benefits, including the following:
Competitive salary, variable compensation, and equity
Broad range of medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees and their dependents, including generous coverage for a platinum PPO healthcare plan
Short-term disability and long-term disability insurance
Cancer and critical illness coverage
Up to 14 weeks paid parental leave (after 1 yr tenure) and childcare FSA plan
401(k) + employer match
Home office set up stipend for fully remote employees
Learning and development support
Generous and flexible vacation and leave policies

jobs.title: Director, Technology Alliances
jobs.text:
Identity has become a critical to an organizations security posture. This is true across their entire digital landscape include cloud, traditional on prem and emerging technologies like agentic ai.Britive is at the forefront of a modern approach to delivering identity security with the only modern privileged access management platform that provides unified Privileged Access Visibility, Dynamic Privilege Management and Secrets Governance across infrastructure, platforms & SaaS.
Our patent-pending technology is deployed at companies of all sizes around the world, including Fortune 500 companies. We have repeatedly ranked among the hottest Cloud Security startups. Britive is founded by CyberSecurity industry veterans with a successful prior exit and is backed by top-tier VCs.
About Britive
Britive is the cloud-native Privileged Access Management (PAM) platform built to secure human, machine, and agentic identities across multi-cloud and hybrid environments. Founded on a Zero Standing Privileges (ZSP) model, Britive replaces static, standing entitlements with just-in-time, ephemeral access — closing off the identity attack surface that traditional PAM and IAM tools leave exposed. Recognized as an architect of Third-Gen PAM, Britive is API-first and built to serve as the identity security control plane for modern, cloud-first enterprises.
Role Summary
Britive is hiring a Director, Technology Alliances to build and lead our technology partner ecosystem across the identity and security landscape. This is a revenue-focused role: the mandate is to identify, prioritize, and build partnerships with technology vendors (IAM, IGA, SIEM/SOAR, cloud security, DevOps/CI-CD, ITSM, and adjacent categories) whose customer bases, integrations, and go-to-market motions can generate measurable pipeline and revenue for Britive — not partnerships that are simply interesting from a technology standpoint.
The ideal candidate brings deep, credible knowledge of the identity and security technology landscape and an established network of relationships with alliance, product, and BD leaders at relevant vendors. They will independently evaluate partnership opportunities against commercial criteria, build the business case and integration requirements for the partnerships worth pursuing, and work cross-functionally with product, engineering, marketing, and sales to bring those partnerships to market.
Key Responsibilities
Partnership Strategy & Prioritization
Maintain a prioritized view of the identity and security technology landscape (IAM/IGA, PAM, SIEM/SOAR, CSPM/CNAPP, ITSM, DevOps/CI-CD, cloud service providers) and identify which vendors represent the highest-value alliance opportunities for Britive.
Score and rank prospective partners against clear commercial criteria — overlapping customer base, co-sell motion, deal size influence, and pipeline/revenue potential — rather than technical novelty alone.
Say no to partnerships that lack a credible path to revenue, even when they are technically compelling, and be able to articulate why.
Deal Development & Business Casing
For each prioritized partner, define and document the value proposition: what joint problem is solved, why customers would buy the combined solution, and how the partnership differentiates Britive competitively.
Author the business requirements for how the two platforms should integrate — use cases, API/data touchpoints, deployment model, and shared customer workflows — in partnership with product and engineering.
Define the monetization model for each partnership (co-sell, referral, OEM/embed, marketplace, technology royalty, etc.) and the commercial terms needed to make it work for both parties.
Negotiate and close partnership agreements, working with legal and finance as needed.
Go-To-Market Execution
Translate signed partnerships into active go-to-market programs: joint solution briefs, co-sell playbooks, enablement for sales and SEs, and marketing campaigns.
Partner with sales leadership to build pipeline generation motions with alliance partners and track sourced/influenced revenue.
Represent Britive at partner and industry events, and build/maintain executive relationships with key alliance contacts.
Cross-Functional Leadership
Act as the primary interface between Britive and partner alliance, product, and BD teams.
Brief product and engineering leadership on partner-driven integration requirements and advocate for roadmap investment where it unlocks revenue.
Report regularly to sales and executive leadership on alliance pipeline, partnership health, and revenue impact.
What Success Looks Like
A short list of active, well-documented technology partnerships — each with a clear value proposition, integration requirements, and monetization model — rather than a long list of loosely-defined technical integrations.
Measurable partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue within the first 6–12 months.
Strong working relationships with key alliance and BD leaders across the identity and security ecosystem.
What You’ll Need
Required Qualifications
7+ years in technology alliances, business development, or partnerships, with at least 3 years focused on identity, security, or adjacent enterprise infrastructure categories.
Deep working knowledge of the identity and security technology landscape — IAM, PAM, IGA, SIEM/SOAR, CNAPP/CSPM, and how these categories intersect with cloud infrastructure and DevOps.
An existing, active network of contacts among alliance, product, and BD leaders at relevant technology vendors.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate partnerships commercially — building business cases, prioritizing against revenue potential, and saying no to low-value opportunities.
Experience defining integration requirements and working directly with product/engineering teams to scope joint solutions.
Experience in a solution design / architecture role listening to and translating client requirements into proposed designs including those with integrations to other products.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting to executives internally and externally.
Willingness to travel for partner and industry events (estimated 20–30%).
Preferred Qualifications
Prior experience at a cybersecurity or identity-focused SaaS company, ideally in a high-growth or startup environment.
Experience building tech alliances from the ground up.
Familiarity with cloud-native and Zero Standing Privileges / just-in-time access concepts.
Existing relationships with hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) marketplace and partner teams.
How to Apply
Interested candidates should submit a resume and a brief note describing a technology partnership they built or led — including the commercial rationale, integration scope, and revenue outcome.
The estimated base salary for this role is $140,000 - $180,000 annually. This position is also eligible for variable compensation tied to the performance of technology partnerships. Individual compensation packages are based on various factors unique to each candidate, including experience, expertise, location, and other factors.
Perks + Benefits:
Work from anywhere in the US! We are fully remote (US only, other areas are subject to review).
Competitive compensation and meaningful equity
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Paid parental leave benefits
401k (U.S.)
Flexible + Unlimited PTO (U.S.)
Career development opportunities and paths
Home office and connectivity stipends
Team socials + Offsites

Score and rank prospective partners against clear commercial criteria — overlapping customer base, co-sell motion, deal size influence, and pipeline/revenue potential — rather than technical novelty alone.
Say no to partnerships that lack a credible path to revenue, even when they are technically compelling, and be able to articulate why.

blocks.text: Deal Development & Business Casing

items: For each prioritized partner, define and document the value proposition: what joint problem is solved, why customers would buy the combined solution, and how the partnership differentiates Britive competitively.

Author the business requirements for how the two platforms should integrate — use cases, API/data touchpoints, deployment model, and shared customer workflows — in partnership with product and engineering.
Define the monetization model for each partnership (co-sell, referral, OEM/embed, marketplace, technology royalty, etc.) and the commercial terms needed to make it work for both parties.
Negotiate and close partnership agreements, working with legal and finance as needed.

blocks.text: Go-To-Market Execution

items: Translate signed partnerships into active go-to-market programs: joint solution briefs, co-sell playbooks, enablement for sales and SEs, and marketing campaigns.
Partner with sales leadership to build pipeline generation motions with alliance partners and track sourced/influenced revenue.
Represent Britive at partner and industry events, and build/maintain executive relationships with key alliance contacts.

blocks.text: Cross-Functional Leadership

items: Act as the primary interface between Britive and partner alliance, product, and BD teams.
Brief product and engineering leadership on partner-driven integration requirements and advocate for roadmap investment where it unlocks revenue.
Report regularly to sales and executive leadership on alliance pipeline, partnership health, and revenue impact.

blocks.text: What Success Looks Like

items: A short list of active, well-documented technology partnerships — each with a clear value proposition, integration requirements, and monetization model — rather than a long list of loosely-defined technical integrations.
Measurable partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue within the first 6–12 months.
Strong working relationships with key alliance and BD leaders across the identity and security ecosystem.

blocks.text: What You’ll Need
Required Qualifications

items: 7+ years in technology alliances, business development, or partnerships, with at least 3 years focused on identity, security, or adjacent enterprise infrastructure categories.
Deep working knowledge of the identity and security technology landscape — IAM, PAM, IGA, SIEM/SOAR, CNAPP/CSPM, and how these categories intersect with cloud infrastructure and DevOps.
An existing, active network of contacts among alliance, product, and BD leaders at relevant technology vendors.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate partnerships commercially — building business cases, prioritizing against revenue potential, and saying no to low-value opportunities.
Experience defining integration requirements and working directly with product/engineering teams to scope joint solutions.
Experience in a solution design / architecture role listening to and translating client requirements into proposed designs including those with integrations to other products.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting to executives internally and externally.
Willingness to travel for partner and industry events (estimated 20–30%).

blocks.text: Preferred Qualifications

items: Prior experience at a cybersecurity or identity-focused SaaS company, ideally in a high-growth or startup environment.
Experience building tech alliances from the ground up.
Familiarity with cloud-native and Zero Standing Privileges / just-in-time access concepts.
Existing relationships with hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) marketplace and partner teams.
